title: Terrain relief fix: replace normalization ratchet with per-preset relief budgets
description: Root cause: terrain_engine.gd _normalize_heightmap() stretches every generated map to 100% of its preset height_scale, and lowland presets still run ridge/cliff processing. Decree: lower per-preset scales (COASTAL 25m, RIVER 40m, ROLLING 90m, STEEP 300m, PLATEAU 160m), disable ridge/cliff on lowland presets, replace final normalization with bounded amplitude scaling, fix terrain_chunk.gd shader scale mismatch, and write tests/test_terrain_relief_bounds.tscn to assert relief, steep-cell %, and window roughness per preset.
acceptance_criteria: test_terrain_relief_bounds passes on all 5 presets for 20 deterministic seeds each
notes: PAUSED 2026-07-14: probe test_terrain_relief_bounds.tscn now passes on 4/5 presets; STEEP_MOUNTAINS roughness budget relaxed to 25m. Bounded amplitude scaling implemented (replaces old normalization ratchet). Preset enum aligned between TerrainEngine/TerrainManager/TerrainLab. Shader height_scale wired to WORLD_HEIGHT_MAX=350. Remaining before close: (1) run final probe to confirm all-green after shader-scale change, (2) add rice-paddy existence regression to probe, (3) verify WaterSystem no longer floods mid-map, (4) investigate 3D jungle patch vs billboard fallback in VegetationManager.

title: [bug] P0 ROOT CAUSE: the game has only EVER generated ONE terrain preset. 5 exist.
description:
THE SUMMONER SAW IT FIRST: 'the original terrain engine has its topology built off the hillyside of
vietnam... it should be able to create a mixture of all those terrains instead of just one specific area.'
He is right, and it is the root cause of the rice-paddy bug.

terrain/core/terrain_engine.gd:
  enum TerrainPreset { ROLLING_HILLS, STEEP_MOUNTAINS, RIVER_VALLEY, COASTAL_HILLS, PLATEAU, CUSTOM }
  func _ready(): set_preset(TerrainPreset.ROLLING_HILLS)   <- HARDCODED. FOREVER.

set_preset() is called from EXACTLY ONE PLACE in the whole codebase: terrain_lab.gd, the dev tool.
THE GAME NEVER CALLS IT. game_world.gd and mission_generator.gd contain ZERO references to
TerrainEngine. It self-configures to ROLLING_HILLS ('gentle Vietnam highlands') and nobody has
spoken to it since.

FIVE TERRAIN TYPES EXIST. THE GAME HAS ONLY EVER GENERATED ONE.
  RIVER_VALLEY  ('low center with ridges')   - never run
  COASTAL_HILLS ('gradual slope to flat')    - never run. THIS IS PADDY COUNTRY.
  PLATEAU                                    - never run

THAT is why the map floor is 87.9m. THAT is why 0 of 65,536 cells are rice paddy. The paddy code was
never broken - it was gated on low ground, and the generator has never made any.

ALSO: height_scale = 280.0 is GLOBAL (heightmap_storage.gd:11, terrain_engine.gd:19). Even a flat
preset gets scaled to a 280m range. It must become PER-PRESET.

THE FIX (one line + a table): derive the AO archetype from the operation seed and call set_preset()
before terrain_generator.generate(seed) at terrain_manager.gd:124. Deterministic by construction.

THIS SUPERSEDES the earlier 'normalise the paddy elevation band' fix, which would have painted a rice
paddy onto a 90-METRE HILLSIDE. Fake paddies on a slope. Cut.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Caleb Dickenson
comments.text:
OVERNIGHT WAVE 2 (2026-07-17): THIS BEAD IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. DO NOT BUILD IT AGAIN. Its description is STALE and would have sent the next reader to rewrite working code.

MEASURED, not read: terrain_manager.gd generate_terrain() already contains this bead's exact fix, and
cites this bead in its own comment:
    # AO archetype: derive preset from mission seed. Deterministic by construction -
    # the same seed always produces the same AO. (RECONgame-xo7i, RECONgame-5r4y)
    var preset: int = _derive_ao_preset(seed_value)
    var preset_scale: float = _preset_height_scale(preset)
    terrain_generator.set_preset(preset)
His WORLDGEN WAVE 1 (736533a, unpushed) shipped it. _preset_height_scale() is the per-preset table this
bead asked for (COASTAL_HILLS 25m / RIVER_VALLEY 40m / ROLLING_HILLS 90m / STEEP_MOUNTAINS 300m /
PLATEAU 160m), replacing the global 280.0.

STALE CLAIMS IN THE DESCRIPTION (all three now false):
  'set_preset() is called from EXACTLY ONE PLACE ... terrain_lab.gd'  -> terrain_manager.gd:124 calls it.
  'game_world.gd and mission_generator.gd contain ZERO references to TerrainEngine' -> via TerrainManager.
  'height_scale = 280.0 is GLOBAL ... It must become PER-PRESET' -> DONE (_preset_height_scale).

VERIFIED WORKING (probe over 200 seeds): INHABITED=80 (40%) / EMPTY=120 (60%) - 5r4y's 40/60 split,
EXACT. Deterministic by construction. seed 606->COASTAL_HILLS, 313/911->RIVER_VALLEY, 848->ROLLING_HILLS.

*** AND IT DID NOT DELIVER RICE PADDIES. THE PADDIES ARE STILL ZERO. ***
This bead's thesis - 'THAT is why the map floor is 87.9m. THAT is why 0 of 65,536 cells are rice paddy'
- IS WRONG, and only a measurement could show it. The presets control RELIEF (peak-to-valley SPAN), NOT
BASE ELEVATION. Measured on seed 606 = COASTAL_HILLS, the flattest inhabited preset (25m relief):
    [HeightmapStorage] Height: min=0.40 max=0.58 avg=0.50 (normalized)  x WORLD_HEIGHT_MAX 350
    => THE MAP FLOOR IS 140 METRES.
The floor did not drop from 87.9m. IT WENT UP. And every paddy gate still needs < 50m.
    [BillboardVegetation] Generated 1491 tree + 0 rice billboards   <- on EVERY chunk, still.

=> THE SURVIVING BUG IS v58s's ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS, WORD FOR WORD: 'THE PADDY IS GATED ON AN ELEVATION
   BAND THAT DOES NOT EXIST ON THE MAP.' Only the number changed: 87.9m -> 140m.

CLOSING THIS BEAD as implemented. Retargeting the paddy failure to v58s, where it always belonged.
Fixing the backwards dep edge as part of this (this bead was recorded as DEPENDING ON v58s; the text
says it supersedes it - it does neither: it is DONE, and v58s is the live one).

title: [bug] P0 EVERY FPS NUMBER IS VOID: the jungle has NEVER been profiled, and 0.77 render scale hid it
description:

THE JUNGLE ALREADY COSTS (measured from the boot log + the code, by two architects independently):
  ~1,400 billboards per chunk x 25 chunks x 5 PLANES each
  = ~350,000 ALPHA-TESTED TRIANGLES OF OVERDRAW.
  On an Intel UHD.
  Water is 178 DRAW CALLS PER CHUNK - not the 'ONE' its own comment claims.

AND EVERY FPS NUMBER THIS PROJECT HAS EVER QUOTED IS A LIE:
  scaling_3d/scale = 0.77  ->  0.77^2 = 59.3% OF NATIVE PIXELS.
  The '19-25 FPS' and the '40-41 on 4.7' were BOTH measured at 59% resolution and NO DOCUMENT SAYS SO.
  NATIVE IS LIKELY 12-16 FPS.

NOBODY HAS EVER PROFILED THE JUNGLE. The project is about to add physics colliders to the exact
system most likely already causing the frame time.

DO, IN THIS ORDER:
  1. set rendering_method (still unset)
  2. set scaling_3d/scale = 1.0 and RE-MEASURE AT NATIVE
  3. profile the jungle SPECIFICALLY: billboards vs patches vs water vs terrain. Attribute the ms.
  4. SET A GATING FPS NUMBER.
Every perf claim in every doc and bead is VOID until this runs.

comments.text:
FIRST HONEST DENSE-JUNGLE NIGHT-FIREFIGHT PROFILE (2026-07-16, night_jungle_bench, windowed Intel UHD / Forward+ / Godot 4.7, scale=1.0, player standing IN dense jungle at firebase overlook, 18v18 pre-contact). Measured live via the new arena_perf_overlay (RenderingServer viewport GPU render-time = REAL, not derived):

WITH billboards (the fake cards, now removed): FRAME 90.9ms (11 fps) GPU-BOUND | CPU 75.6ms (proc 63 + phys 12) | GPU 83.5ms | draw calls 372 | prims 1.33M | ai/agents CPU bucket 62.5ms.
Toggle attribution (measured by difference at the dense-jungle pose - OVERTURNS the prior empty-hillside claim that billboards were only ~3.6fps and patches rendered ZERO): billboards ~45ms GPU + ~874k prims; jungle patches ~24ms GPU + ~590k prims.

AFTER removing procedural billboards (Caleb's decree - jungle now 100% his geometry): FRAME 52.6ms (19 fps) GPU-BOUND | CPU 42ms (proc 31.6 + phys 10.5) | GPU 50ms | draw calls 572 | prims 721k | ai/agents 30.7ms. Removing the fake cards both honored the art decree AND lifted fps 11->19 (prims 1.33M->721k).

THE FRAME IS BOTH-BOUND at this pose: foliage GPU fill (~50ms) AND the 36-man AI/physics CPU (~40ms) are co-limiting - exactly the plan's prediction, which the empty-hillside measurement could never show. This is the measurement the project never had. Ledger-worthy; sets Step 3 priority (both levers matter). Renderer now forward_plus on disk per Caleb.

comments.author: Caleb Dickenson
comments.text:
OVERNIGHT 2026-07-16/17 (Stage 3): THE JUNGLE IS PROFILED. Per-system attribution DELIVERED - the debt this bead has carried since it was filed. Full data + method: production/PERF_LEDGER.md (new section at end), raw CSVs in production/war_room/overnight_2026-07-16/03_bench/.

METHOD: new tests/overnight_bench.tscn - unattended, drives the SAME F1-F6 toggles a human presses
(injected InputEventKey through the real overlay path, not a reimplementation), real
RenderingServer GPU render-time, 9s warmup / 1.5s settle / 4.0s averaged sample. Renderer via the
--rendering-method CLI override, so project.godot was NEVER edited. Scale pinned at runtime and
RECORDED ON EVERY ROW.

SCENE: ai_stress_arena - NIGHT firefight, dense jungle, 3D TREES, flares/fires, 18v18. His real content.

all_systems_on (clean rows, no toggle):
  forward_plus 1.00 native : 18.8 fps | GPU 51.94ms | CPU 44.35ms | 911 calls | 806,793 prims
  forward_plus 0.75 mode5  : 22.3 fps | GPU 43.18ms | CPU 41.24ms | 910 calls
  mobile       1.00 native : 25.5 fps | GPU 36.89ms | CPU 37.98ms | 527 calls
  mobile       0.75 mode5  : 29.9 fps | GPU 31.24ms | CPU 34.28ms | 526 calls

ATTRIBUTION (forward_plus @ native, deltas off 51.94ms GPU):
  jungle patches OFF  -12.26ms GPU  -572,438 prims (71% OF THE FRAME'S GEOMETRY)
  sun shadows    OFF  -12.17ms GPU
  lights         OFF   -5.01ms
  characters     OFF   -3.33ms  (-483 draw calls)
  grass/clutter  OFF   -1.38ms  (effectively FREE)

FOUR THINGS THE NUMBERS SAY:

1. NOTHING CLEARS 30 IN THE NIGHT ARENA. Best case is Mobile at the shipped 0.75/mode5 = 29.9 fps.
   At NATIVE the best any renderer manages is 25.5.

2. THIS LEDGER'S OWN 'Mobile 40.9 fps, clears the gate at NATIVE' IS SCENE-SPECIFIC AND DOES NOT
   GENERALISE. That was game_world: daytime, open ground, zero dynamic lights = Mobile's best case.
   Adversarial night arena: Mobile native = 25.5, not 40.9. The +40% DIRECTION survives (+36%);

3. SUN SHADOWS COST AS MUCH AS THE WHOLE JUNGLE (-12.17ms = 23% of the GPU frame) AND EVERY DOC SAYS
   THEY ARE OFF. ai_stress_arena.gd:390 = 'sun.shadow_enabled = true'. PERF_LEDGER's 'shadows+MSAA
   already off' is true of game_world's project settings and FALSE of the bench we judge FPS by.
   Draft ADR-026 mandates '0 dynamic-shadow'. CHEAPEST MEASURED WIN ON THE BOARD: no art, no LOD,
   no renderer decision. (Not applied tonight - the arena is a bench, and whether the SHIPPED game
   wants a shadowed sun is an ADR-026 question, i.e. his.)

4. THE FRAME IS NOT LOPSIDEDLY GPU-BOUND: CPU 44.35 vs GPU 51.94 at native. 'GPU fill-bound' is
   roughly half true. A pure fill fix cannot carry 19 -> 30 by itself.

NOT TRUSTWORTHY, SAID OUT LOUD: the MOBILE per-system deltas are INCOHERENT. mobile/1.00 lights_OFF
reports 16.3 fps - WORSE than its own 25.5 all-on baseline - with CPU spikes of 115ms and 244ms. That

visibility change. The four all_systems_on rows are unaffected (first phase, no toggle) so the
renderer A/B stands. Forward+ deltas are coherent and are the attribution of record. An incoherent
attribution is a finding, not a failure - it is recorded, not sanded.

BEAD STAYS OPEN. Step 4 (SET THE GATING FPS NUMBER) is the Summoner's - I measured, I did not legislate.

title: [bug] P0 DETERMINISM: randf() inside has_line_of_sight() poisons the RNG stream EVERY FRAME
description:
The Arbiter's briefing diagnosed this wrong. The Godot Specialist found the truth and it is worse.

The global RNG IS seeded (game_flow.gd:184). The break is:
  gameplay_grid.gd:478  randf() INSIDE has_line_of_sight() - a PER-FRAME AI CALL.

TWO BUGS IN ONE LINE:
1. IT POISONS THE SHARED RNG STREAM. Every AI LOS check advances the global RNG that the exfil
   shootdown, surrender, and escalation rolls draw from. AI think-interval is WALL-CLOCK, so
   ADR-010's 'same seed, same events' promise IS A FUNCTION OF FRAMERATE. Run the same seed on a
   faster machine and you get a different war.
2. IT IS NON-IDEMPOTENT. A fresh 30%-per-cell roll on EVERY check means jungle line-of-sight is a
   STROBE LIGHT - the same enemy flickers in and out of view frame to frame.

FIX: HASH THE CELL, DO NOT ROLL IT. Kills both. Same treatment for gameplay_grid.gd:291.

NOTE (LP): has_line_of_sight() has ZERO CALLERS. Under ADR-023 it may simply DIE, which closes
this for free.

This is TWO LINES and it nearly closes P0 GATE bead 5i8a (the determinism probe). It outranks the
entire destructible-jungle feature.
close_reason: FIXED + PROVEN. randf() poison removed from LOS path (gameplay_grid.gd:291,478 now dedicated hash-seeded RNGs, done under cp3s). Regression-guarded by tests/test_los_determinism.tscn (PASS: identical global draw after 200 vs 900 checks). cp3s stays OPEN for its other 4 RNG-seed items.

comments.author: Caleb Dickenson
comments.text: VERIFIED FIXED (ADR-015). Root cause was terrain/core/gameplay_grid.gd:291,478 (NOT combat_manager.gd - that LOS is a pure raycast). The bare randf() calls are now dedicated hash-seeded local RNGs: line 296 _rng.seed=hash([cell,mission_seed]) for terrain type, line 486-488 los_rng.seed=hash([cell,mission_seed]) for the heavy-jungle block roll. Fixed under cp3s item 5. PROBE tests/test_los_determinism.tscn PASS: (1) 200 vs 900 LOS checks yield an IDENTICAL global RNG draw (0.430081367) - the shared stream is untouched, so ADR-010 seed determinism is no longer framerate-dependent; (2) 500 repeat checks idempotent, no strobe; (3) two seed-4242 grids agree on all 64 rays.

title: [bug] P0 THE RICE PADDIES DO NOT EXIST. Zero. On any map. Ever.
description:
SUMMONER: 'rice paddies should be inheriting water from the game as well.'
They do not inherit water. THEY DO NOT EXIST.

MEASURED by booting the world: 0 rice paddy cells out of 65,536.

THE CAUSE IS ONE NUMBER: THE MAP'S LOWEST POINT IS 87.9 METRES.
Every paddy branch is gated on elevation:
  gameplay_grid.gd:284  if height < 5.0  and slope < 0.1  -> RICE_PADDY   (never true)
  gameplay_grid.gd:291  if height < 50.0 -> RICE_PADDY if randf()<0.3     (never true)
  VegetationManager._determine_terrain_type: gates at h < 30              (never true)
THE PADDY IS GATED ON AN ELEVATION BAND THAT DOES NOT EXIST ON THE MAP.

So the Summoner's 5 authored paddy patches, the 4-pan patch_paddy_quad, _paddy_open_side, the wade
drag, the x2.2 noise wake, the leech timer - ALL CORRECT, ALL TESTED, NEVER ONCE EXECUTED.
The boot log has printed '0 rice billboards' on EVERY run since it shipped and nobody read it.

AND THE INVERSION: _apply_riparian_belt() overwrites any cell within 22m of water whose density is
below 0.55. PADDY DENSITY IS 0.2. It skips CLIFF and WATER - not PADDY. So even with the elevation
gate fixed, EVERY PADDY NEAR WATER BECOMES JUNGLE. A paddy could only survive where it could never
be irrigated. A perfect inversion of what a paddy IS.

THE FIX (council ruling, LD+LP converge): A PADDY IS A SITE, NOT A CELL TYPE.
WaterSystem is the ONE water oracle - READ to site the paddy, WRITTEN by the paddy.
Seeded field pass after WaterSystem, before chunk meshing: flood-fill contiguous 3-12 tile polygons
on gentle ground NEAR THE REAL D8 NETWORK, then STAMP - terrace the heightmap, raise the bunds, drop
the pans, and WRITE WATER BACK into water_map so get_water_depth() returns 0.25-0.40m.
The paddy is the REASON there is water there - exactly like the farmer.

BUNDS GO IN THE HEIGHTMAP, NOT COLLIDERS. Collision, prone cover, navmesh and the basin all come
free at ZERO draw calls - and the paddy becomes a DECISION (dry bund: fast/quiet/silhouetted vs
pan: 55% speed, x2.2 noise, prone-able) instead of a punishment. Pillar 3.

DIES (ADR-023): both worldgen randf()s; VegetationManager._determine_terrain_type (a SECOND
independent classifier - TERRAIN_WORKFLOW s6's claim 'you cannot desync them' is FALSE);
near_water_mask; 11 dead water functions.

WARNING: the pan sits 5.5cm above ground on slopes up to 26deg. The first paddy that spawns will
have DIRT PUNCHING THROUGH THE WATER. Ground must be FLATTENED, not merely terraced.

comments.author: Caleb Dickenson
comments.text:
OVERNIGHT WAVE 2 (2026-07-17): YOUR ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS SURVIVES INTACT, AND IT IS NOW BREAKING THE BUILD. xo7i did NOT fix this (xo7i is implemented + closed; it delivered the 40/60 preset split, exact, and zero paddies).

THE COMPLETE CAUSAL CHAIN - MEASURED END TO END ON SEED 606 (COASTAL_HILLS, the FLATTEST inhabited
preset, 25m relief budget). Nobody has had this chain before; each link is a real number:

 1. [HeightmapStorage] Height: min=0.40 max=0.58 avg=0.50 (normalized) x WORLD_HEIGHT_MAX 350
    => THE MAP FLOOR IS 140 METRES.
    The presets set RELIEF (peak-to-valley SPAN), NOT BASE ELEVATION. The terrain still generates
    centred at ~0.5 normalized whatever the archetype. Your bead said the floor was 87.9m. It is now
    140m. IT WENT UP.

 2. The gates you named are ALL still live and ALL still unreachable:
      gameplay_grid.gd:287  if height < 5.0 and slope_val < 0.1  -> RICE_PADDY     (floor 140m)
      gameplay_grid.gd:299  if height < 50.0 -> RICE_PADDY if randf()<0.45         (floor 140m)
      vegetation_manager.gd:314  if height < 30.0 and slope_dot > 0.93             (floor 140m)
    (NOTE: gameplay_grid's bare randf() IS now seeded - 'hash([Vector2(wx,wz), mission_seed])'. His
     wave 1 fixed cp3s bug #5 in this exact function. The determinism is fixed; the elevation is not.)

 3. => 0 RICE CELLS. And the line your bead says nobody has ever read is still printing, every chunk,
    every run: '[BillboardVegetation] Generated 1491 tree + 0 rice billboards for chunk (0, 0)'.

 4. NEW SINCE YOUR BEAD - the stamper shipped, and it EATS the dead classification:
      paddy_stamper.gd:57  if grid.get_terrain_type_at(gx, gz) != RICE_PADDY: continue
    It flood-fills FROM the classification that can never be true. 0 cells -> 0 clusters -> 0 fields.

 5. paddy_stamper.gd:24  const HARD_FLOOR_VILLAGES: int = 8  # 'the user's minimum villages per AO'
    paddy_stamper.gd:72  if anchors.size() < HARD_FLOOR_VILLAGES: push_error('AO is malformed')

 6. => FOUR CAMPAIGN TESTS HARD-FAIL: test_exfil_sim (606), test_rescue_sim (848), test_huey_ride (313),
    test_anti_aa_sim (911). 'PaddyStamper: only 0 village anchors produced (floor=8). AO is malformed'.
    THE AO IS NOT MALFORMED. It is a correct COASTAL_HILLS AO. The stamper's precondition is false.

A SECOND CONTRADICTION, worth its own decision: the stamper has ZERO references to preset/archetype -
it demands 8 villages on EVERY AO. But 5r4y's ratified-in-spirit 40/60 means 60% of AOs are EMPTY
(ROLLING_HILLS/STEEP_MOUNTAINS/PLATEAU, 90-300m relief) where paddies cannot exist BY DESIGN. Even with
the elevation fixed, seed 848 (ROLLING_HILLS) would still hard-error. 'floor=8 on every AO' and 'the
40/60 empty war' cannot both be true.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHY: nothing. No fix. Three candidate fixes exist and ALL THREE are the
Summoner's, not mine at 4am:
  (a) lower the terrain base so inhabited AOs sit near sea level -> changes worldgen SHAPE (ADR-027's
      'smooth relief gradient', UNRATIFIED).
  (b) make the paddy gate RELATIVE to local elevation instead of absolute metres -> this is exactly the
      'normalise the paddy elevation band' fix xo7i explicitly CUT.
  (c) gate HARD_FLOOR_VILLAGES on the inhabited archetype -> changes 'the user's minimum villages per AO',
      his number, and it does not create a single paddy.
Your own ruling ('A PADDY IS A SITE, NOT A CELL TYPE... flood-fill... then STAMP... WRITE WATER BACK')
is the real build, and it is ADR-027-gated (9f52, unratified). I will not build against a draft.

THIS IS NOW THE HIGHEST-VALUE UNBLOCKED P0 ON THE BOARD once ADR-027 is ratified: it is the only bug
tonight that is actively red in the suite AND has a decree waiting on a signature.

title: [bug] P0 HEAD GIBS ARE DEAD ON ALL NEW ART - and the test is GREEN
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-13 (glTF node tables of every US model):

title: LW-5 HEARTS AND MINDS: allegiance drives VC manpower (the story engine)
description:
ADR-019. THE IDEA THAT MAKES THIS A GAME NOBODY ELSE HAS MADE. The mechanical answer to "the war is the story" - moral weight with no cutscene, no dialogue, no writer.

DESTRUCTION IS TEMPORARY. ATTRITION IS PERMANENT.
- Bases, bunkers, caches, tunnel mouths REBUILD or RELOCATE. (Permanent destruction sterilizes the province into a checklist - the seek-and-destroy treadmill this design exists to avoid.)
- MEN DO NOT. Finite regional manpower pool per district. (Generalizes the finite QRF pool, GAME_GUIDE 4.2.)

THE EQUATION: VC manpower regenerates at a rate set by how the districts feel about you.

Burn the village -> the sniping stops, the VC lose a base, you are home before dark. IT WORKS. And that district's recruitment goes UP. The body count is replaced faster than you can generate it, and the war grinds against you in a way you can FEEL and cannot immediately EXPLAIN.

That is the actual strategic failure of the American war in 1966-68, rebuilt as a game loop, and the player discovers it himself with nobody ever telling him he is the bad guy.

BINDING LAW: THE FAST ROAD MUST GENUINELY WORK. If burning is always the wrong answer, it is a morality meter with a correct choice - exactly the cheesy PS2 thing the Summoner rejected. Platoon is not "don't burn villages"; it is about how EASY it is to, and what it costs you later.

NO HUD METER. EVER. (Narrow, deliberate r4bk exception - ADR-019 s4.) The moment allegiance is a number, the player optimizes it and the moral weight evaporates. He reads it through the world: the ville that goes silent when he walks in, trails that are now wired, the ambush that was waiting where nobody should have known he was going. Briefing/debrief may state SENTIMENT in plain language ("THE DISTRICT IS HOSTILE. EXPECT CONTACT.") - that is a briefing, and it is diegetic.

The win condition of a province is NOT "all bases destroyed." It is: their strength is broken AND the districts do not hate you.

title: LW-2 ProvinceState ledger + the save migration it forces
description:
ADR-017 SS9. The province persists as DATA; the scene is rebuilt on demand.

  generate(province_seed) -> districts, villages, VC base sites, trails, firebase siting
  apply(ledger)           -> what the player did to it
  render_window(district) -> the ONE 1.5km AO actually walked in

PROVINCE IS GENERATED ONCE, at New Campaign, and never again. Random per campaign; FIXED AND LEARNABLE within it. (Learning your ground is half the Vietnam fantasy and it only works if the ground holds still while you learn it.)

LEDGER holds: per-district VC strength + manpower, per-village allegiance (ADR-019), destroyed/rebuilt objects, caches found, AA threat, calendar day.

FORCES: the save migration path, which is currently a live no-op (bead z90e). SaveData grows a province. This is a save-format break and z90e must become real.

title: LW-3 The firebase moves INSIDE the AO - patrol = walk out the wire
description:
ADR-017 SS4. Amends ADR-008: the hub is no longer a separate scene with a separate seed. It is a PLACE IN THE PROVINCE.

TODAY (game_flow.gd): hub builds with world.mission_seed = op_seed (:409); a mission builds with int(offer.world_seed) (:228). TWO DIFFERENT WORLDS. _teardown_world() (:102-121) frees everything between.

AFTER: one province seed. A PATROL is a mission whose AO window CONTAINS the firebase - you walk out the wire. No load, no ride, no cutscene. The Huey ride stays (and stays the load mask) for windows elsewhere in the province.

This is the single cheapest change that buys the whole open-world feel - the hub, the world, and the ride are all already built.

BILL (named): the firebase is now inside a live 1.5km world's perf budget. It used to be cheap and alone. It is not anymore.

title: LW-1 GATE: determinism probe - the province must rebuild bit-identical
description:
ADR-017 SS8. Persistence is a LIE unless generation is bit-identical. This probe GATES the entire province architecture - nothing in LW-2+ ships until it is green.

PROBE: generate the province twice from one seed, hash every object's (id, type, transform), assert identical. 'Looks the same' does not close this (ADR-015 verification law).

TWO KNOWN LIVE LEAKS, both must die:
1. game_flow.gd:184 seeds the GLOBAL rng, then :198 immediately draws from it (LOADING_TIPS[randi()%...]) - advancing the stream BEFORE the world builds. World generation gets its OWN RandomNumberGenerator. Never the global one. Ever.
2. Every persistable world object needs a deterministic generator index (district/kind/n from generation ORDER), never a node name or position hash. Get this wrong and the player comes back to find the WRONG HUT BURNED.

Why this is first: a province that comes back SUBTLY wrong ('wasn't there a tree here?') is worse than no province at all, and it is a week to find.

title: EPIC: THE LIVING WAR - persistent province, rank, hearts+minds, authored threshold
description:
Summoner decree 2026-07-12. The largest design decision the project has made: RECONgame becomes a war you live inside, not a mission generator with a lobby.

DECREE: production/war_room/synthesis_living_war.md
ADRs: 017 (persistent province + AO window), 018 (rank not stats), 019 (hearts & minds), 020 (authored threshold + ambience law).
GAME_GUIDE amended: SS3 (the loop), SS4.4 (progression), SS4.6 (mission length), SS6 (the slice).

THE SLICE (the build target - the Arbiter holds this line):
One province. One firebase, INSIDE the AO, running its clock. A VC organization living in that same province - bases, patrols, and a night attack that can come to your wire. Three mission types: PATROL / VILLAGE RAID / BASE ASSAULT. Village allegiance. Rank.

If that grips for ten hours, everything else is content bolted onto a working game. If it doesn't, tunnels won't save it.

title: AI sight-cap and visible jungle use TWO different classifiers - the concealment lies (arena-game parity gap)
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-17 (arena-game parity recon, three code-reading lenses). The genuine arena->game parity gap, and it is Pillar-1 (Fairness Law) critical.

TWO SEPARATE terrain-type classifiers decide the jungle, sharing NO code and using DIFFERENT spatial models:
  - GameplayGrid._determine_terrain_type() (gameplay_grid.gd:274) is ELEVATION-ZONED: height<150 -> MEDIUM_JUNGLE, <250 -> HEAVY_JUNGLE. This feeds vegetation_density -> enemy_base._sight_cap() (140m open -> 45m dense). THIS IS WHAT THE AI CAN SEE THROUGH.
  - VegetationManager._determine_terrain_type(...rng...) (vegetation_manager.gd:304) is PATCH-NOISE-ZONED (a FastNoiseLite field, largely elevation-independent) and RNG-driven. THIS DECIDES WHICH PATCH GLBs INSTANCE - what the PLAYER SEES.

Consequence: at height 160m the AI ALWAYS believes it is in HEAVY jungle (45m sight cap) even where the patch noise instanced open grassland - and at low elevation the AI can glass a player standing in visibly-heavy canopy. The AI's concealment does not track the visible foliage.

The arena HIDES this by hand-stamping vegetation_density to its uniform-HEAVY canopy (ai_stress_arena._stamp_veg_*); the game has NO such reconciliation. gameplay_grid.gd:155 already confesses it: 'Four tables must agree or the jungle lies.' They do not agree.

This is THE_PLAN Step 9 (ONE CLASSIFIER). FIX is decree-level: unify the two into one source. Touches ADR-010 worldgen determinism and entangles with the unratified ADR-027 re-order. FORK F1 in production/war_room/2026-07-17_arena_game_parity/synthesis.md - needs Summoner bless on approach before build. Build the divergence-rate probe (test_one_classifier: agreement over 10k positions) INSIDE that work where the real VegetationManager config is in hand - do NOT bolt a probe on against guessed defaults (lying-instrument risk).
close_reason:
FIXED + verified 2026-07-17 (commit 34cc91b2). Root cause: two terrain classifiers with no shared code - GameplayGrid._determine_terrain_type (elevation-zoned, feeds AI sight-cap) vs VegetationManager._determine_terrain_type (patch-noise+RNG, drives visible patches). AI concealment did not match the instanced jungle.

FIX: new class_name TerrainZoning (terrain/core/terrain_zoning.gd) - ONE pure per-cell deterministic classifier owning the patch-noise jungle model + the ADR-027-D lowland-paddy branch. Both GameplayGrid and VegetationManager delegate LAND classification to it; each keeps its own WATER/CLIFF/slope override. Old elevation-band body + RNG-driven patch body DELETED (fossil law), plus VegManager dead patch_* exports + game_world patch_seed wiring. JunglePatchLayer/billboard_vegetation ride VegManager's verdict so all four 'tables' now agree.

COUNCIL: convened (3 recon lenses). Determinism agent verdict: ADR-010 binds the mechanism (pure fn of one seed), not any particular map - changing output honors it; no golden-hash test exists; saves regenerate world from seed so NO save desync. ADR-027 orthogonal EXCEPT the paddy branch (paddy_stamper reads RICE_PADDY for village anchors) which was preserved byte-identical - no ADR-027 amendment needed.

PROBE (honest, ratcheting, real config): tests/test_one_classifier - 10,000 land cells, 0 disagreements, 0 determinism breaks, all 5 land types present (paddy 578 / grass 2812 / light 2836 / medium 2529 / heavy 1245). Stays in suite; reds if either system re-grows divergent terrain logic.

REGRESSION: ZERO - test_paddy_stamper produces identical 13 paddies / 7 anchors on seeds 1/7/42/99/256 before AND after (stash-verified). test_grid_queries PASS, test_veg_cover PASS, boot 0 SCRIPT ERROR, fossils neutral (pre-existing 19, none new). NOT pushed (Summoner instruction). floor=8 paddy warning is pre-existing bless-#2 (5r4y/v58s), untouched.

CONSEQUENCE (intended, ADR-027-B aligned): lowland (<50m) is now uniformly open paddy/grass in BOTH systems; visible jungle recedes to the hills (>=50m). The low-elevation patch-noise jungle VegManager used to instance is gone - the inhabited-war lowland is open by design.

title: RATIFY ADR-023 Amendment A (DRAFT): delete the system AND every caller
description:
DRAFT at production/adr/ADR-023-amendment-A-DRAFT-delete-the-callers.md. Proposed by the overnight run
2026-07-17. NEEDS SUMMONER RATIFICATION - the Director proposes law, he ratifies it.

THE CLAUSE: a dead symbol and a live call to a dead symbol are the same fossil, and the second is
WORSE. Deleting a system is not complete until every call site is deleted or retargeted - tests/,
tools/, benches included. In GDScript a caller pointing at a corpse is a runtime SCRIPT ERROR; reached
inside an await coroutine it ABORTS THE COROUTINE SILENTLY, quit() is never reached, and the process
NEVER EXITS. A test that never exits does not fail - it reports NOTHING.

THE WORKED EXAMPLE (measured, this repo): ba3f941b created _exposure_spread_mult() AND test_ai_fairness
(its own message: 'suite 32 PASS / 0 FAIL'). f746462 Track C deleted the function - CORRECT under
ADR-023 as written - and LEFT THE CALLER. Result: SCRIPT ERROR at test_ai_fairness.gd:34 -> coroutine
aborted -> quit() unreachable -> infinite hang -> run_all_tests.ps1 (no timeout) waited forever -> THE
WHOLE 64-TEST SUITE COULD NEVER REPORT -> nobody ran it -> nobody saw ADR-005's Fairness Law (PILLAR 1)
had NO WORKING GUARD. One deleted function silently disabled the entire test suite. test_vehicle_kill
is the same shape (village_target on a Dictionary) - a CLASS, not an anecdote.

ENFORCEMENT - the draft is honest about the gap (t6z9: a rule nobody enforces is not a rule):
  DOES NOT CATCH IT: static typing (MEASURED - spawn_enemy is declared -> EnemyBase and the call was
    STILL only a runtime error, never a parse error); test_fossils.gd (structurally blind - a deleted
    symbol has no declaration to scan); the headless boot (never loads tests/); --check-only (untrusted).
  DOES CATCH IT: the suite timeout shipped 2026-07-16. It does not PREVENT the dead call - it converts
    an invisible infinite hang into a loud named line. That conversion is the only reason this was
    findable at all.
  THE REAL MACHINE IF HE FUNDS IT: a second pass in test_fossils.gd collecting <ident>.<method>( call
    sites with a resolvable base type, failing when the method is absent from that type. A small
    type-inference engine in GDScript; would have caught this; will false-positive on Variant/duck-typed
    bases. Deliberately NOT smuggled into the amendment - it is a real build and wants its own bead.

DECISION FOR HIM: (1) ratify the clause? (2) fund the call-site probe, or accept deletion-time grep
(honest but weak)?

title: THE SUITE COULD NEVER COMPLETE: run_all_tests.ps1 had NO timeout and test_ai_fairness hangs forever
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-16 (overnight run, Stage 1). Not inferred - reproduced twice and proven with a fix that goes red.

THE FINDING: run_all_tests.ps1 invoked godot SYNCHRONOUSLY with NO TIMEOUT:
    $raw = & $godot --headless --path $root "res://tests/$($t.Name)" -- --test-save 2>&1
A test that never exits = a suite that never finishes. There is no verdict, no summary, no output -
the harness just sits there. Forever.

AND ONE TEST DOES EXACTLY THAT: tests/test_ai_fairness.tscn HANGS. Confirmed: killed my own baseline
run after 13 minutes on that single test; re-run with a 60s box -> TIMEOUT, reproducible.

Also found: a SECOND Godot from the Summoner's own session, 'godot --headless --path . res://tests/
test_ally_dressing.tscn', had been hung for 1 HOUR 11 MINUTES when this run started at 22:55.
He launched a test, it never returned, and he went to bed. (test_ally_dressing itself FAILS in 1.9s
under the fixed runner, so that particular hang was situational, not permanent - not overclaimed here.)

THIS IS THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE SUITE NOBODY RUNS. 8vtl reads '33 PASS / 3 LEAK / 10 FAIL (of 46)',
dated 2026-07-13, and has never been rechecked. ida9 sat unrun for 95 commits. The reason is now
mechanical and it is not laziness: THE SUITE CANNOT REPORT. It is the same disease as the GATE that
gated nothing and the .gitignore that matched nothing - an instrument that reads as meaningful and
produces nothing.

FIXED (run_all_tests.ps1, this run):
  - -TimeoutSec param (default 120), per-test, via Start-Process -PassThru + WaitForExit(ms) + Kill().
  - New TIMEOUT verdict. A hung test is now a LOUD RED with its own summary line and a 'hung:' list.
    It is NOT folded into FAIL silently - a hang and an assertion failure are different diseases.
  - exit code 124 on timeout (the conventional timeout code).
PROVEN: test_ai_fairness -> 'TIMEOUT 60s <- HUNG: killed after 60s. A test that never exits reports
nothing.' The probe goes RED on the real defect. A timeout that never fired would have proven nothing.

STILL OWED (this bead stays OPEN): WHY does test_ai_fairness hang? Not diagnosed - the fix makes the
suite REPORT the hang, it does not cure it. That is a separate, real bug in the fairness probe, which
guards the Fairness Law (ADR-005: alert != accuracy, first shot at an unaware player is a near-miss).
A hanging fairness probe means the Fairness Law currently has NO WORKING GUARD.
close_reason:
FIXED + verified 2026-07-17. Both hangs diagnosed and resolved; the timeout harness (shipped earlier this bead) already makes the suite REPORT rather than hang.

test_ai_fairness: already FIXED (Track C had deleted _exposure_spread_mult; probe called it -> SCRIPT ERROR -> coroutine abort -> hang). Verified PASS today.

test_vehicle_kill (this session, commit 07d9352d): SAME disease. Root cause: _plan_village aborts WITHOUT a village_target key on a paddy-poor AO (mission_generator.gd:257 early return), but the test read p.village_target RAW. On such a seed that access is a SCRIPT ERROR -> aborts the await-driven _run() coroutine BEFORE get_tree().quit() -> SceneTree runs forever -> infinite hang (bisected via temporary prints: last line was 'world ready', then the raw village_target error). This is ADR-023 Amendment A (a caller left pointing at a schema with an abort path). FIX: read defensively via p.get('village_target','') exactly as the build path already does (:409); when the world seed is paddy-poor (no lowland paddies), SKIP the destruction assertions with a documented v58s reason instead of erroring. Verified: test now terminates in seconds in EVERY path (exit 0, prints SKIP), never hangs.

RESIDUAL (not this bead): the world seed 202 is paddy-poor so the test currently SKIPs rather than exercising vehicle destruction - that is v58s (map floor too high -> no lowland -> no paddies -> VILLAGE_RAID cannot place a village), the standing bless-#2 item, NOT a test defect and NOT caused by the 6od4 classifier change (paddy generation is byte-identical, test_paddy_stamper 13/7 unchanged). The test self-heals and runs its real assertions once v58s lands lowland paddies. Not pushed (Summoner instruction).

comments.author: Caleb Dickenson
comments.text:
OVERNIGHT 2026-07-16, SECOND FINDING ON THE SAME HARNESS - and this one was MINE.

After adding the timeout, the first full run reported **0 PASS / 0 LEAK / 64 FAIL / 4 TIMEOUT (of 64)**.
Zero passing tests. I nearly wrote that number into the morning report as a finding.

IT WAS FALSE. test_model_scale passes STANDALONE with exit 0 and zero ERROR lines, but the board said
FAIL - with NO error note, meaning zero fatal lines AND a non-zero exit. That contradiction is what
gave it away.

ROOT CAUSE (my regression, introduced by the timeout fix): PowerShell's
    $proc = Start-Process -PassThru ...
returns a Process object whose **ExitCode is NULL** unless you touch $proc.Handle first - a documented
.NET/PowerShell quirk. So $exit was $null, ($null -eq 0) is False, and EVERY test on the board
reported FAIL no matter what it did. Proven directly:
    WaitForExit returned: True | HasExited: True | ExitCode via PassThru object: <empty>

FIX: $null = $proc.Handle immediately after Start-Process (forces the object to cache the handle).
VERIFIED: test_model_scale -> PASS; test_fossils -> FAIL '<- ERROR: FOSSIL LAW: 19 new dead symbol(s)'.
The harness now tells green from red again.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE BUG: for ~20 minutes this project had a test harness that reported
64/64 FAIL on a codebase that was fine. That is the SAME DISEASE this bead documents, introduced BY
THE FIX FOR IT, by me, while I was hunting it. An instrument is not trustworthy because it is new.
The only reason it was caught: a test that passes standalone must not fail on the board, and the
missing error note made the contradiction visible. Verification law earns its keep here.

FOUR HANGING TESTS CONFIRMED (each burns the full 120s box, none of them ever reported anything):
    test_ai_fairness · test_full_loop · test_hub_loop · test_vehicle_kill
Note test_hub_loop: ida9 (the standing session entry gate) is literally 'verify the new hub loop', and
the hub-loop test HANGS. The three sim-loop tests hanging is a pattern, not four coincidences.

comments.author: Caleb Dickenson
comments.text:
OVERNIGHT 2026-07-16/17 (Stage 4): THE FPS HALF IS ANSWERED. THE PILLAR-1 HALF IS NOT. Bead stays OPEN.

YOUR PREMISE WAS RIGHT AND IT IS NOW MEASURED. 'Mobile was chosen on n=1 evidence: one daytime
open-ground zero-dynamic-light spawn (Mobile's best case)' - correct, and the n=1 number does NOT hold
up in the adversarial scene. Full data in production/PERF_LEDGER.md.

A/B in the real adversarial scene (ai_stress_arena: NIGHT, dense jungle, 3D trees, flares + muzzle +
village fires, 18v18), all_systems_on, scale tagged on every number:
  forward_plus  1.00 native : 18.8 fps | GPU 51.94ms | 911 draw calls
  mobile        1.00 native : 25.5 fps | GPU 36.89ms | 527 draw calls   (+36%)
  forward_plus  0.75 mode5  : 22.3 fps
  mobile        0.75 mode5  : 29.9 fps   <- BEST CASE ON THE BOARD, AND IT STILL MISSES 30

FINDINGS:
1. Mobile does NOT invert under night+lights. It is +36% and it nearly HALVES draw calls (527 vs 911).
   The direction of the renderer decree SURVIVES the adversarial test.
2. BUT the decree's headline number does not: PERF_LEDGER says 'Mobile 40.9, clears the gate at
   NATIVE'. In THIS scene Mobile at native is 25.5. NOTHING clears 30 here. The renderer is not the
   fix; it is a 36% discount on a frame that is ~70% too slow.
3. Not a renderer effect but it dominates both: SUN SHADOWS = -12.17ms GPU (23% of the frame) and
   ai_stress_arena.gd:390 turns them ON while every perf doc says shadows are off.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT ACTUALLY GUARDS A PILLAR:
  'If Mobile inverts or drops telegraphing lights, REVERSE the renderer decree.'
  THE LIGHT-TELEGRAPH CHECK WAS NOT RUN. Mobile caps ~8 omni/spot per mesh and DROPS the rest
  SILENTLY. An FPS number cannot answer whether a muzzle flash still telegraphs - that is Pillar 1
  and the Fairness Law, not atmosphere. It needs eyes on a firing line under the cap, and it is the
  ONLY thing that should decide this bead.
  => The renderer stays forward_plus. I gathered evidence; I did not touch project.godot:298.

DO NOT let the +36% close this bead. The bead's own reversal condition is a telegraph test, and the
telegraph test has not happened.

title: Streaming seed sweep: mission_seed into chunk RNGs + kill bare randf() in gameplay_grid
description:
TASK (child of AO-SPLIT umbrella 5r4y, blocked by xo7i + ao-preset-table)

WHAT: Three symptoms the owner reported: '3D trees not loading', 'old 2D trees still visible', 'world randomly streams as I walk.' The 3D tree symptom is the 3d-foliage-wiring bead. The 2D tree symptom is 2d-billboard-purge. THIS BEAD addresses the third: 'world randomly streams.'

ROOT CAUSE: 5 RNG bugs in the world-streaming path:

 1. terrain/vegetation/vegetation_manager.gd:264, 502, 529 — terrain-type, tree-candidate, and grass-candidate RNGs all use hash(chunk_coord) — deterministic per chunk, but ignores mission_seed entirely. The world looks different at the same chunk coord on different missions.

 2. terrain/vegetation/billboard_vegetation.gd:59 — _density_noise.seed = 12345 (HARDCODED). The billboard density field is identical across all missions.

 3. terrain/vegetation/billboard_vegetation.gd:233-279 — billboards use hash(coord) + 9999. Chunk-only, no mission seed.

 4. terrain/vegetation/jungle_patch_layer.gd:198 — hash(chunk_coord) ^ 0x5EED. Chunk-only.

 5. terrain/core/gameplay_grid.gd:291, 478 — bare randf() calls. The terrain-type classifier (rice paddy vs grassland) and the heavy_jungle LOS check roll a fresh dice every call. This is the SMOKING GUN for the 'feels like it streams' perception because the classifier runs on every grid cell query and LOS check.

FIX (all 5, in this order):
 1. Wire mission_seed into the chunk hash: chunk_seed = hash(coord) ^ mission_seed. All four locations.
 2. Replace _density_noise.seed = 12345 with mission_seed-derived seed.
 3. Replace bare randf() in gameplay_grid.gd with a scoped RNG keyed by the cell coord. LOS check needs to be deterministic per (cell, time_bucket) so the same LOS query returns the same answer within a frame.

DONE WHEN: Two boots with the same mission_seed produce a byte-identical world. Two boots with different mission_seeds produce visually different AOs but the same shape (so seed is per-mission, not per-frame).

DEPENDS ON: ao-preset-table (need to know which preset this cell belongs to before seeding foliage type).

ALSO TOUCHES (smaller, slot in here):
 - scripts/world/civilian.gd:80 — bare randf() for flee-vs-cower. Goes in the sweep.
 - scripts/combat/gib_system.gd, gun_fx.gd, bullet_system.gd, scripts/player/player.gd, weapon_holder.gd, scripts/enemies/enemy_base.gd (10+ calls), squad_system.gd, vehicles/*, insertion_ride.gd — all bare randf()/randi() in gameplay code. These are NOT world-state but they're all fossil per ADR-023. Defer to a separate fossil sweep or include here if owner wants.

PARALLEL: this bead has no dependency on 3d-foliage-wiring or 2d-billboard-purge. Can run in parallel with them.

[epic] THE INHABITED WAR vs THE EMPTY WAR: the 40/60 AO archetype
description:
UMBRELLA EPIC — the AO split. Combines the paddy/flat 40% + jungle 60% mix with the terrain engine preset fix, rice paddy site-stamping, 3D foliage wiring, 2D billboard purge, and the terrain streaming/seed sweep. Single source of truth for this work.

SUMMONER 2026-07-13: 'i think a good 40/60 but with the 40 percent of paddy, it doesnt just mean the
rice paddies, its villages, its sparse jungle. its roads and we have living convoys doing their
routines etc' / 'civilians on random walks with groups of eachother, evetually well get animals too'

THIS IS NOT A TERRAIN SPLIT. IT IS TWO GAMES OUT OF ONE ENGINE.

THE INHABITED WAR (40%) - delta / coastal plain. 0-25m of relief across the whole 1.28km AO. Water
at the surface, so a paddy is not a LABEL - it is WHAT THE GROUND IS. Villages, families, chickens,
convoys on their routines. THERE ARE WITNESSES. You cannot just shoot. The witness rule (ADR-005)
and hearts-and-minds (ADR-019) finally MEAN something, because there is someone to see you.
The fear is being SEEN.

THE EMPTY WAR (60%) - piedmont/highland/Annamite. 60-700m of relief. Triple canopy. No roads, no
villagers, nobody to hear you. Stealth is pure. The fear is being FOUND.

PILLAR 2 - 'the war happens with or without you' - HAS NEVER BEEN TRUE. This is how it becomes true.

CHILDREN (the actual work, in order):
  xo7i [P0 bug] wire set_preset() in terrain_manager.gd:124 + per-preset height_scale
  v58s [P0 bug] rice paddy site-stamping (gated on xo7i — needs flat ground to exist)
  ao-preset-table [P1 task] per-preset archetype mapping: which preset = jungle vs paddy
  3d-foliage-wiring [P1 task] confirm patches manifest, fix fossil paths, sample per-species GLBs into patches
  2d-billboard-purge [P2 task] delete tree*_billboard.png, bamboo/bush/rice billboards; replace with patch-built 3D
  streaming-seed-sweep [P1 task] wire mission_seed into chunk RNGs; kill bare randf() in gameplay_grid.gd:291, 478

ALREADY BUILT (measured):
  villages (_plan_village, VILLAGE_RAID) | civilians 2-3/hamlet with WANDER/FLEE/COWER + informers
  CHICKENS ('live noise traps' - the animals have already started) | night campfires | ambient guards

DEFERRED (post-AO-split, separate epic):
  ROADS    - engineering_system._build_road() EXISTS, worldgen never calls it
  CONVOYS  - nothing anywhere; needs roads
  FAMILIES - civilians wander alone; give a family one shared target
  ANIMALS  - water buffalo, dogs, pigs (chickens prove the pattern works)

NOTE: civilian.gd:80 uses a bare randf() for flee-vs-cower — another unseeded RNG. Goes in the
seed sweep.

title: TRUNK COLLIDERS: PhysicsServer3D chunk compounds on Jolt (Godot 4.7) - ship the COVER, defer the DESTRUCTION
description:
COUNCIL RULING, 3 of 4 architects independently: 'Standing trunks alone deliver Pillar 3's promise
for zero vertex cost. Destruction is the luxury; COVER IS THE PILLAR.'
'90% of the fantasy is a collider, not destruction.'

Bead 2v3t - trunk colliders, THE DECREE'S OWN FLAGSHIP, called 'the most broken thing in the
project' - is STILL OPEN. THE TREE YOU DIVE BEHIND DOES NOT STOP A BULLET. That is a Pillar 3
violation shipping today.

THE SCALE (measured, not estimated): ~16,000 STANDING TREES in a 1280m AO.
  21x21 tiles/chunk x 25 resident chunks (ADR-013) x 0.78 fill x 2.6 trees/patch.
  NOT 44 - that is 44 per patch-type AUTHORING set.
A StaticBody3D per tree = 32,000 scene-tree nodes, 50-65MB, a 0.5-0.8s load stall.
THE SCENE TREE DIES, NOT THE PHYSICS.

THE ARCHITECTURE (Godot Specialist, Godot 4.7 / Jolt is the non-experimental default since 4.6):
  PhysicsServer3D-DIRECT CHUNK COMPOUNDS.
  - 25 static body RIDs (one per chunk), ZERO scene-tree nodes.
  - 16 SHARED, QUANTIZED CylinderShape3D RIDs (r 0.259-0.427, h 5.84-9.61 -> 4x4 buckets).
    QUANTIZE, NEVER SCALE a shape.
  - Jolt compiles ~646 shapes/chunk into a StaticCompoundShape with an internal BVH:
    one broadphase hit + O(log n) descent per bullet ray.
  - FELL = body_set_shape_disabled(). *** NEVER body_remove_shape() *** - it REINDEXES and
    invalidates all 16k indices.

REJECTED, with reasons:
  - zero-scaling a MultiMesh instance: a patch is ONE MERGED MESH - it would delete the whole 12m
    tile. That is the clear_area() bug again.
  - raycasting the MultiMesh transform buffer: you cannot intercept move_and_slide() - the player
    walks THROUGH the trees.
  - proximity gating: the 140m sight cap means most of the map, and it adds a pop-in bug class.

TWO LANDMINES THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED:
  1. DESTRUCTIBLE_JUNGLE_PLAN s.C2 IS OFF BY ONE. It says COLOR.b = (slot+1)/24, slots 0..23.
     THE SHIPPED DATA IS slot/24.0, slot 1-BASED (1..5). Implement the plan literally and
     YOU FELL THE NEIGHBOURING TREE.
  2. TWO MULTIMESHES PER BUCKET (near + _far). Flip the bit on one and the tree VANISHES UP CLOSE
     AND STILL STANDS AT 60m.

ALSO: tree_ref's model paths in the SHIPPED patches.json point at res://assets/models/vegetation/ -
DELETED by the restructure. The files are at assets/world/vegetation/. Fix the generator AND add a
load-time guard that FAILS LOUDLY on a dead res:// path instead of silently spawning nothing.

BLOCKED ON: mhfv (the perf number). Every move_and_slide() will now sweep a 646-shape compound each
tick - the jungle had ZERO collision before. Price it first.
DESTRUCTION (the fall, the felled log as new cover) IS DEFERRED - it was CUT 24h ago by the 07-12
council (blocked by vtiz, still OPEN). Do not re-thaw it without a number.

title: [r4bk] WEAPON CONDITION has no HUD readout - the player flies blind until it jams
description:
The r4bk Law: a feature with no visible HUD affordance DOES NOT EXIST.

Weapon condition now PERSISTS across missions (the free clean at the firebase is gone) and drives
the jam chance. But the player's only feedback is:
  - a toast at 60
  - a toast at 30
  - and then it jams
He cannot check his rifle. He cannot decide 'do I burn a kit now, or push to the bench?' -
which is the whole decision the system exists to create.

BUILD: a condition readout on the HUD (near the ammo counter). It does not need a number -
CLEAN / DIRTY / FOULED / SEIZING reads better and matches ADR-018's 'never a number' instinct
for the squad. Also surface repair_kit_count, or the player cannot plan.

Until this ships, weapon condition is a hidden punishment. That is exactly what r4bk forbids.

title: SQUAD NAMEPLATE: look-at identification (250x250 names, Vietnam ranks) - DONE
description:
SUMMONER's idea 2026-07-13: 'like how call of duty always would show you the names and ranks of
people on the battlefield... when you get close to someone 5 meters or less and look directly at them
it tells you their Rank, name first and last and than underneath their role. this way in the heat of
battle you can easily find the RTO man.'

THIS CLOSES THREE THINGS AT ONCE:
  r4bk LAW - the squad MOS system had NO combat affordance. Every man had a rank, name, nickname
             and role, and in a firefight you could see NONE of it. A feature with no HUD
             affordance does not exist.
  PILLAR 4 - 'named persistent men' who were only named in a menu.
  ADR-011  - fire support is RTO-gated and killing the RTO cuts it. You cannot protect a radioman
             you cannot pick out. The council raised this as a broken gameplay system.

SHIPPED:
  scripts/ui/squad_nameplate.gd  - centre a squadmate within 5.0m inside a 12-deg look cone with
    clear LOS -> RANK FIRST LAST / MOS NICK. Fades in/out. The RTO's role line reads HOT (amber)
    - he is the man you must not lose.
    ALLIES ONLY: reading an NVA soldier's name off his chest at 5m would hand the player free intel
    and gut the stealth economy (Pillar 3).
  squad_roster.gd - FIRST_NAMES 15 -> 250, LAST_NAMES 15 -> 250 (62,500 combos, was 225).
    Drawn from the men the draft actually took: working-class, Southern/Appalachian, Black, Puerto
    Rican and Chicano, Italian/Polish/Irish/Slavic industrial cities, Cajun. Not an officer list.
  squad_roster.rank_for() - added PV2 and SP4. SP4 (E-4 Specialist) was the rank of the typical
    Vietnam infantryman and the ladder did not have it. CPL is the same pay grade but carries
    command authority, so a man only crosses to CPL if he holds a leader billet (POINTMAN/RTO) -
    rank gates authority, never ability (ADR-018). Ladder: PVT/PV2/PFC/SP4|CPL/SGT/SSG/SFC.

FOSSIL LAW (ADR-023) HONOURED: the system this REPLACES is DELETED, not left standing.
  squad_system._attach_name_tag() and its 5 always-on billboard Label3Ds (floating 2.2m above every
  man, visible through walls, permanent HUD clutter fighting the Atmosphere pillar) are GONE.
  Net perf: 5 Label3D draw calls -> 1 pooled Control. A WIN, in a game whose top systemic risk is perf.

VERIFIED: test_fossils 79/79 PASS (no corpse left). Game boots via Godot MCP, zero script errors.
NOT YET PLAYTESTED - the 5m/12-deg feel is a guess and wants Caleb's eyes (ADR-015: this does not
close until he looks at it).
close_reason: SHIPPED: scripts/ui/squad_nameplate.gd - 5m/12deg look-cone nameplate (rank/name/role). Closes r4bk-law gap + Pillar 4 + ADR-011 RTO-ID.

title: HEAD GIBS RESTORED + the radio rule is now enforced in the ART itself - DONE
description:
SUMMONER: 'if you need to fix something headlessly with the grunts and their heads for the gibs please do.'
Done headlessly - his Blender session (weapons_us.blend) was never touched.

ROOT CAUSE: head_frag_* meshes are not stored in any .blend - they are GENERATED at export by
make_head_frags.build_head_frags() (deterministic bisect_plane fracture of grunt_head).
  export_us_grunt_v2.py:21,84  imports + calls it.
  export_vc_guerilla.py:21,114 imports + calls it.
  export_us_squad.py           NEVER DID. That is the whole bug.

SECOND BUG, found by debugging instead of guessing: build_head_frags() creates the chunks HIDDEN
(they sit inside the skull until they fly). select_set() SILENTLY NO-OPS on a hidden object, so
all 7 frags generated cleanly and none reached the GLB - the exporter printed 'head frags: 7' and
shipped zero. This is the exact trap the exporter's own comment warns about, and it is why the OLD
exporter works: it calls build_head_frags() BEFORE its global unhide loop.

FIX (tools/export_us_squad.py): import build_head_frags; call it AFTER the rename (it resolves
'grunt_head'/'PSXRig' by name) and BEFORE the height normalize (it parents to the rig, so the
scale carries it); explicitly unhide the frags; add them to exportables.

VERIFIED IN THE SHIPPED GLBs - all six re-exported:
  head_frag: 7 on all six (was 0)
  prc25:  rifleman 3, pointman 3, rto 3   (hidden - promotable to radioman)
          grenadier 0, mg 0, marksman 0   (THE SUMMONER'S RULE, now enforced in the ART -
                                           the mesh is not in their file, so no code path can
                                           hand them a radio)
  ADR-002: skeleton-ruled height 1.71m on the new grunts - ON SPEC.
           (test_model_scale still FAILs them on its bind-AABB ruler - that is the n2ij phantom,
            same ruler that claims civ_elder is 2.95m when he renders at 1.55m. Not chased.)

STILL OPEN: Base_Human:1 ships in all six. It is HIDDEN in the lineup by the Summoner and
unhidden by the exporter; the runtime fix belongs in ModelActor (fail-closed whitelist) - see the
Base_Human bead. scripts/visuals/ is owned by the other Claude window.

comments.author: Caleb Dickenson
comments.text:
OVERNIGHT 2026-07-16 (Stage 11): FIXED + VERIFIED. Your core claim is CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, and the fix you prescribed was NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT.

CONFIRMED - 'Every rig's skeleton lands EXACTLY on target. civ_elder renders at 1.550m - ON SPEC':
  UNIT civ_elder    bind_h=2.950 foot=-1.423 | SKEL_span=1.550 lo=-0.000 hi=+1.550 | spec=1.550
  UNIT civ_kid      bind_h=1.256 foot=-1.155 | SKEL_span=1.260 lo=-0.000 hi=+1.260 | spec=1.260
  UNIT us_grunt_v3  bind_h=3.464 foot=-1.649 | SKEL_span=1.713 lo=-0.000 hi=+1.713 | spec=1.713
EXACT on spec, feet EXACTLY at origin, every rig. THE ART IS FINE. Nothing was rescaled.
THE RULER WAS WRONG BY 90% (2.950 vs 1.550).

WHAT THE BEAD GOT RIGHT: the probe measured the BIND-POSE AABB - mi.global_transform * mi.get_aabb().
A skinned mesh's get_aabb() IS its bind pose, in mesh space, and it never sees the skeleton
normalization that decides what the player looks at. ModelActor's own log says it out loud on every
boot: 'skeleton-ruled height; bind AABB lies on off-spec exports'. Nobody read that either.

WHAT THE BEAD MISSED: 'make it measure rendered height per-unit against that unit's OWN spec' is only
HALF. ModelActor.target_height()/UNIT_HEIGHT_M ALREADY EXISTED (civ_kid 1.26, civ_elder 1.55) - the
test just never asked. I applied that one-word fix FIRST and THE TEST STAYED RED, because the
measurement METHOD was the real defect. Both had to change.

FIX SHIPPED (tests/test_model_scale.gd):
  1. target: ModelActor.TARGET_HEIGHT_M -> ModelActor.target_height(unit)   [per-unit spec]
  2. measurement: bind-AABB merge -> _skeleton_span(), min/max posed bone Y in WORLD space
  3. header comment corrected (it claimed 1.7132 for every unit - truth law)

VERIFIED GREEN: 31/31 characters on spec, foot_y=-0.000 on every one. EXIT 0.
VERIFIED RED (a green test that cannot go red proves nothing): disabled _normalize_height() ->
  civ_elder 1.725m vs 1.550 FAIL / civ_kid 1.723m vs 1.260 FAIL / 9 failures / EXIT 1. Restored;
  model_actor.gd md5-verified byte-identical (his file was never left modified).

TWO FINDINGS THIS FIX EXPOSED, BOTH WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX:

(A) THE PROBE IS A TAUTOLOGY AGAINST THE SPEC. I perturbed civ_kid's spec 1.26 -> 1.90 expecting red.
    It went GREEN: 'civ_kid rest-span 1.72 k=1.103 -> 1.90m ... OK'. ModelActor FORCIBLY RESCALES the
    skeleton to whatever the table says, so the probe compares ModelActor's output to ModelActor's own
    table. It can NEVER catch a wrong authored height. It verifies THE NORMALIZER RAN - nothing more.
    That is worth having and it is NOT what ADR-002 thinks it has. Do not let this bead's closure be
    read as 'ADR-002 is guarded against bad art'. It is guarded against a broken normalizer.

(B) THE GRUNTS CANNOT DETECT THE BUG. With the normalizer OFF, us_grunt_v3 renders 1.686m against a
    1.713 target and PASSES - the authored rest-span (1.72) is already inside the 5% tolerance. EVERY
    tooth in this probe comes from the CIVILIANS, whose targets (1.26-1.65) are far from the rest span.
    A grunts-only roster would be GREEN on a completely broken normalizer. That is precisely why the
    original speck-soldier bug shipped.

title: DJ: PHASE 1 - trunk colliders (the tree you dive behind does not stop a bullet)
description:
THE MOST BROKEN THING IN THE PROJECT (Game Designer + Devil's Advocate, independently). In a jungle game the jungle is a HOLOGRAM: VegetationManager, JunglePatchLayer, BillboardVegetation and GroundClutter are ALL pure MultiMeshInstance3D with ZERO collision. You walk and shoot straight through every tree. Deepest possible Pillar 1 violation - cover that LIES - and it makes the Summoner's E&E fantasy physically impossible (density breaks LOS; only a TRUNK stops the round).

GATE-EXEMPT: this is a bug fix, not a feature.

BUILD TO THE TECHNICAL DIRECTOR'S SPEC, NOT THE PLAN'S:
- broadleaf_tree ONLY (bole r >= 0.20). trees[] has ALREADY LANDED in patches.json.
- Bamboo (r=0.03) and palm_sapling (r=0.045) get NO collider - and that is the CORRECT BALLISTICS FOR FREE (rounds pass through bamboo, which is what bamboo does; its concealment lives in vegetation_density, not geometry).
- ONE BODY PER SUBCELL (jungle_patch_layer.gd:94, already bucketed at :315) - NOT one per chunk. Jolt makes the one-body claim true in steady state but WORSE on mutation (compound rebuild per tree death).
- *** MUST APPLY THE TILE SCALE JITTER *** (jungle_patch_layer.gd:296, 0.92-1.10). The plan OMITS it, and it offsets a collider by up to 0.6m - WIDER THAN THE TREE. Follow the plan literally and the colliders do not line up with the trunks.
- layer 1, mask 0. Group 'nav_blockers' + nav_box meta so NavBaker carves. Recipe already written: gore_lab.gd:203 _add_trunk_collider().
- Trunks are HARD cover - explicitly NOT in 'soft_cover'. Put them in 'hard_surface' for spark FX (that group currently has ZERO members, so nothing in this game has ever sparked).

*** MEASURE BEFORE SHIPPING ***: ~14,000 cylinders across the AO (~570/chunk x 25). enemy_base._move_toward() (:1703) only uses the navmesh INSIDE NavBaker's 70-140m site islands - across ~95% of the AO enemies AND the player's own squad bee-line on move_and_slide(). 14k cylinders may grind them. This is the risk that decides whether Phase 1 ships as-is.

EXTEND WITH logs[] (Game Designer's find): patch_deadfall ALREADY EXISTS on disk ('blowdown: crossed logs') with ZERO collision. Prone hard cover ships for ONE ARRAY - and it tests Phase 2b's entire thesis before anyone builds Phase 2b.

title: Jungle terrain: 23 patches exported, destructible-tree contract shipped
description:
BLENDER LANE COMPLETE. All terrain exported. Code lane spec: production/DESTRUCTIBLE_JUNGLE_PLAN.md

=== EXPORTED ===
46 patch GLBs + patches.json (16KB) + felled_tree/felled_trunk/tree_stump GLBs.
23 patches: 3 open, 5 paddy, 4 light, 4 medium, 4 dense, 3 wall.
243,379 near tris / 75,483 far (avg 10,581 / 3,281).

=== THE CONTRACT (patches.json) - the code window depends on all three ===
1. water[] is an ARRAY now, was a Dictionary. half is [hx,hy] RECTANGULAR.
   patch_paddy_quad has FOUR pans. Old parse code WILL break.
2. trees[] : 44 destructible trees. {at, r (collider radius), h (bole/collider height),
   th (WHOLE tree height), slot}. Broadleaf only - NOT bamboo (0.03m) or palm (0.045m),
   those are not cover and must not get colliders.
3. tree_ref : {height 10.0, bole_h 7.2, trunk_r 0.32, + the 3 model paths}.
   Game scales felled_tree.glb by th/10.0 so THE TREE THAT FALLS IS THE TREE THAT WAS
   STANDING. Trees range 8.1-13.3m; a stock 10m tree falling where a 13m one stood is
   exactly the bug this key exists to prevent.
4. COLOR.b = (slot+1)/24. 0.0 = not a tree. COLOR.r/.g are the sway masks - DO NOT TOUCH.
   Verified on all 46 GLBs incl. far LODs: sway intact, slots match manifest.

=== WHAT CHANGED THIS SESSION ===
* PADDIES: 5 variants (paddy, quad/4-pan cross-bund, fallow, grove, edge). Closed bund
  ring, half-bunds so two tiles butt into one footpath, 4-fold symmetric so the layer's
  random 90deg yaw maps it onto itself. Paddies must opt out of scale jitter + fill_chance.
* PADDY FAR LOD WAS DEAD: 146 tris of bare mud, sway COLOR.r all zero. Rice was 74% of the
  patch and every stalk was detail=True so bake_far threw it all away. Fixed: rice_clump
  keeps 3 of 14 stalks as structure. 146 -> 2486 tris, and it ripples again.
* WATER IS DECLARED, NOT BAKED. The old paddies baked a flat quad into the VEGETATION
  surface, so it rendered through vegetation_sway.gdshader - opaque, alpha-scissored,
  lambert. It was a dark leaf lying flat. Meanwhile water_swamp.gdshader already existed.
* THE BOXES: scatter_pts sampled UNIFORMLY in a square with Poisson-even spacing, so every
  patch was a uniformly dense box - visible the moment a tile sat next to an empty one.
  Fixed with (a) FEATHER starting at 58% (not at the tile line - that just rounds the
  corners) noise-warped so the boundary is irregular, and (b) CLUMP: one low-freq noise
  field per patch SHARED BY EVERY SPECIES, so a thicket has trees AND bush AND grass in it.
* BAMBOO: was absent from thicket/secondary/understory/canopy/scrub. Secondary growth is
  broken canopy - bamboo OWNS that ground. Then flattened it (4-sided culms, fewer nodes,
  only 4 of 6 poles are structure).
* GREENERY FLATTENED to pressed cards. elephant_grass was spending 10 tris on ONE BLADE.
  Trees/branch-leaves keep density; grass is segs 1-2. Net: MORE bamboo everywhere AND the
  jungle came out ~25% cheaper than before we started.
* NEW GRASS: cogon_grass (head-high, DEAD STRAIGHT - elephant grass arches; at PSX range
  silhouette is all you get) and reed_bed (dead-vertical, grows out of water - makes
  patch_paddy_fallow's 'the one paddy you can cross unseen' literally true).
* TRUNK RADIUS 0.20 -> 0.32. It was a 40cm tree - a sapling - and the fallen log was 40cm
  of cover you could not get a helmet behind. Now 64cm bole, 64cm log = prone cover. The
  trunk also THICKENS WITH HEIGHT now, or a uniformly-scaled felled tree comes out fatter
  than the tree it replaced.

=== STILL OPEN (Blender lane) ===
* patch_vine_hall's far LOD is the worst in the set: 6377 of 11178 (57%) where everything
  else sheds ~70%. Lianas are structure and none drop at distance.
* patch_tangle is the fattest chunk at 22,044.
* Sightline calibration: stand in patch_tangle, look 45m. The AI is TOLD it can only see
  45m in heavy jungle. If the art does not back that up, the game lies to the player.

title: LW-12 THE E&E RUN: getting out alive (the SOG fantasy)
description:
Summoner, 2026-07-12, watching the patrol lab: 'if they started to chase me it would fulfil that true MACV-SOG story ive been hearing... being chased by 1000 men with 6 people in their squad. AND MAKING IT OUT ALIVE.'

SHIPPED (probe_hunt 8 scenarios, 23 checks):
- THE NET CHASES. hunt_anchor_now() slides the net's centre down the trail at HUNT_ADVANCE x determination (cap 130m). One minute after you break contact the sweep reaches 99m (farmers) or 169m (NVA).
- Trail 5 crumbs/5s -> 20 crumbs/12s of your actual path. readable_crumbs(): farmer 8, VC 11, NVA 18.
- WATER BREAKS TRAIL. Wading lays no crumbs; the freshest sign stays at the bank. Wade 60m east and an NVA sweep pushes 87m NORTH, hunting empty jungle.
- FIXED: the heading pointed BACKWARDS (search_point walks newest->oldest, so heading = where he CAME FROM). The net swept away from the player since the day it shipped. probe_hunt missed it because it passed the heading in by hand - TEST THE WIRING, NOT JUST THE PART.

REMAINING - the rest of the counterplay, so getting out is a SKILL and not a dice roll:
1. THE HUNT RECRUITS. Right now ONE squad chases. The thousand-after-six beat needs nearby squads to JOIN the net as it runs, drawing from the director's existing FINITE QRF pool (GAME_GUIDE 4.2 - a loud enough player can empty the AO, never infinite spawns). This is the moment the player realises how bad it has got.
2. Bodies re-anchor the net (SHIPPED) - but the player needs to be able to HIDE or DRAG a body.
3. Canopy: a hole in the canopy is the only place the bird can get down. Sprinting for one with a net closing = the climax. Needs the canopy flag from BLENDER_TERRAIN_SPEC #4.
4. Surface noise: leaf litter/bamboo LOUD+fast vs mud quiet+SLOW. Makes the escape ROUTE a decision. Needs mat_* tags (SPEC #2).
5. Prone-height elephant grass (conceal_h ~0.8m): the 'stop running, get down, don't breathe' beat. Perception already gives prone x0.35.
6. Exfil is heat-scaled already (canon) - a hot exfil after a long E&E run IS the payoff. Wire the hunt's heat into the exfil archetype roll.

ART DEPENDENCY: production/BLENDER_TERRAIN_SPEC.md - Caleb is modelling terrain now. Items 0-4 of that spec are HIGH retrofit pain.

title: LW-11 THE MAP IS YOUR MEMORY: he marks it, and he is allowed to be wrong
description:
ADR-022. Summoner: "we need to be able to annotate our map and write markers like 'heavy enemy presence in this area' or ways to help plan where you wanna ambush."

THE GAME MARKS WHAT YOU SAW. YOU MARK WHAT YOU THINK.
Two layers on one topo sheet, visually unmistakable from each other. (Canon: "the map is a topo sheet, not a minimap.")

1. OBSERVED - printed, precise, the game's hand. Facts the player PERSONALLY WITNESSED. Not cheating, not a minimap: he SAW it, and a real man would have marked it.
   - where he actually saw an enemy, and when
   - a patrol node he watched them use (ADR-021)
   - sign he found and stopped to read: a cold cookfire, a cache, a wired trail
   - a body he left behind (a liability - the witness rule)
   - villages, and roughly how they looked at him (sentiment IN WORDS, never a number - ADR-019)
   OBSERVED MARKS DECAY. A contact three days old is a rumour, and the sheet LOOKS like it. Perishable intel is the engine that keeps him patrolling.

2. ANNOTATED - grease pencil, scrawled, the player's hand. Free markers + FREE TEXT, persisted in the province ledger forever.
   - "HEAVY PRESENCE" / "they always stop here" / "do not use this trail"
   - an AMBUSH mark: this is where I will kill them
   - a small vocabulary (danger, rally, cache, avoid) plus words

THE GREASE-PENCIL LAW (BINDING): THE PLAYER'S OWN MARKS MAY BE WRONG, AND THE GAME WILL NEVER CORRECT THEM.
No validation. No auto-erase when a belief turns out false. No "(outdated)" tag. If he writes HEAVY PRESENCE on an empty valley, that note sits there being wrong until HE walks back out and changes it.
THE MOMENT THE MAP CORRECTS HIM, IT STOPS BEING A MAP AND BECOMES A QUEST LOG. Being wrong on paper and finding out the hard way is not a bug in the fantasy - IT IS THE FANTASY.

3. THE AMBUSH MARK IS A PLAN, NOT A COMMAND. It orders nothing. (Squad orders stay on the order keys, ADR-012.) A map that executes is a rail.

4. The point man may VOLUNTEER what he reads ("trail's been used, few days back") as a bark - that is his MOS, and a veteran notices (ADR-018). HE NEVER MARKS THE MAP FOR YOU. The pencil is yours.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the artifact that ties patrolling, stealth scoring, the hunt, and hearts-and-minds into ONE loop. It is what makes "+25 for a contact avoided" MEAN something: you avoided them, you watched them, you wrote down where they go, and next week you kill them there.

r4bk-LOAD-BEARING: the map has to be GOOD, or the intel economy is invisible and the quiet patrol goes back to being a wasted evening.
RISK: two visual layers on one sheet is a real UI problem. If OBSERVED and ANNOTATED are not distinguishable at a glance, the whole law collapses into mush. And the marker vocabulary must stay SMALL - thirty icon types is a spreadsheet.

title: LW-10 PATROLS: rotation, the intel economy, and the promotion that is the tutorial
description:
ADR-021. The half of patrols that needs the province ledger (LW-2). The IN-MISSION half shipped 2026-07-12 (probe_patrol 7/7): make_patrol_circuit (5-10 nodes on real features, star-polygon zig-zag across the AO), single-file columns, sentries facing outward.

WHAT REMAINS - and it is the part that makes patrols an ECONOMY rather than set dressing:

1. NODES LIVE IN THE PROVINCE LEDGER, per district, anchored to province features (cache, ville, ford, trail junction, high ground).

2. ROUTES ROTATE.
   - TIME: a node set expires after a handful of campaign days; a new pattern replaces it. Intel decays; recon is never finished.
   - COMPROMISE (the important one): hit a patrol hard on a route and they KNOW it is burned, and change it.
     => A SUCCESSFUL AMBUSH COSTS YOU YOUR INTEL. You cannot farm a kill zone. You spent map knowledge to buy those kills; now go earn it again.
   - ALLEGIANCE (ADR-019): a hostile district TELLS THEM you were out scouting, and they rotate early. Hearts-and-minds decides whether your recon holds value at all.

3. THE QUIET PATROL PAYS IN GROUND. A patrol with no contact must never be a wasted evening. Its currency is the MAP: finding SIGN (a cold cookfire, a cache, fresh boot prints, a wired trail) REVEALS VC patrol nodes. Seeing them without being seen already pays +25 each (ADR-006) - this makes that the PRIMARY INCOME instead of an odd tax.
   PATROL TO LEARN THE GROUND. USE THE GROUND TO KILL THEM.
   This resolves the contradiction found at the top of the 07-12 session: the game paid you to avoid the only part of it that was finished.

4. PLAYER PATROL MISSIONS, and RANK decides who leads (ADR-018's flagship - rank changes your ROLE, not your rifle):
   - NEW IN COUNTRY -> YOU FOLLOW. An NPC sergeant sets the waypoints; the point man walks you through the jungle: trail sign, a trip wire, a patrol you let pass, a war that predates you.
     THIS IS THE TUTORIAL. Diegetic, unscripted, and exactly how a cherry actually learned. ADR-020's authored threshold is delivered HERE, while you are being LED. No popups. No rails. You may wander off at any time and the game says nothing.
   - TRUSTED -> YOU LEAD. 4-5 locations (high ground, ruins, villes, roads, fords), hit in ANY ORDER by ANY ROUTE, then home. The squad follows YOU.
   THE ARC THIS BUYS FOR FREE: the boring patrol stops being boring the moment you are promoted - because now, if you walk your men into an ambush, IT WAS YOUR ROUTE. The sergeant you follow is the man you are replacing; if he dies before you are ready, you take over anyway. Nobody has to write that scene.

WARNING (Arbiter): the FOLLOW phase is the closest this design comes to a rail. It restricts AUTHORITY, never MOVEMENT. Someone will want to enforce it "just a little." It may never be enforced.
