title: LW-9 THE MOVING WAR: emergent battles, doors you can walk through, a horizon you cannot
description:
ADR-020 s3.3. Summoner, 2026-07-12: "i do want to have the player come across other larger battles from time to time while they are out and about... NOT JUST ALL BIG BATTLES ARE STAGED... somethings yes should be caged from us, that makes the distance seem larger... but there should be random events like STUCK CONVOYS IN AN AMBUSH, or a TRAPPED SQUAD."

THE WAR MOVES WHETHER HE SHOWS UP OR NOT.

A. THE MOVING WAR (the coarse strategic sim - this is what makes the battles EMERGENT rather than staged)
   The province ledger carries UNIT TOKENS, not just static sites. A few dozen, moving on the DISTRICT map, at campaign tempo (per day, not per frame):
   - VC/NVA: resupply runs down the trail net, tax-collection circuits, massing for an attack, displacing after you hit them
   - Friendly: US patrols out of the firebase, ARVN outposts, convoys on the dirt roads (the roads already exist - GAME_GUIDE 4.9)
   Where two tokens COLLIDE, a battle EXISTS. It resolves on its own if nobody comes. If the player's AO window happens to CONTAIN one, it is LIVE and he can walk into it.
   This is cheap: it is tokens on a data map, not simulated soldiers. It is also what makes the war COHERENT - the QRF he dodged last week is a company that is now massing, and next week it comes to his wire (LW-7).

B. THE DOORS (reachable, joinable, refusable - ADR-020 s3, class 2)
   Stuck convoy in an ambush. A squad pinned and calling on the net. An ARVN outpost being overrun. A downed bird.
   - He can JOIN, AVOID, or WATCH AND WALK ON.
   - They appear on NO BRIEFING. They are opportunities, not objectives.
   - This extends the existing "contact deck" already in GAME_GUIDE 4.6 ("contact deck gives the AO ambient jobs").
   - ADR-020's BINDING TEST still governs: he must be able to LEAVE, right now, with the game neither stopping him nor punishing him.

C. TWO TRAPS, AND THE RULES THAT KILL THEM
   TRAP 1 - "the side-quest chore." If helping ALWAYS pays, it is a checklist, and every door becomes a tax on his time. RULE: helping COSTS (ammo, blood, the clock on his own mission - and his own mission's objectives do not pause) and pays UNPREDICTABLY: sometimes intel, sometimes a survivor who joins the roster, sometimes nothing but the fact that they lived.
   TRAP 2 - "the chaos map." If a door is always open, we have built the rival game's constant Battlefield chaos, which the Summoner explicitly rejected. RULE: doors obey the AMBIENCE LAW (LW-7). RARE. A big battle should be a thing he TELLS SOMEONE ABOUT, not a thing he expects.

D. THE MIRROR OF HEARTS AND MINDS (the good, dark idea)
   Allegiance (ADR-019) tracks how the VILLAGES feel about him. This tracks how HIS OWN SIDE does.
   Driving past a pinned American squad is ALLOWED. The game says nothing. It is never scored.
   But the firebase KNOWS. It comes back as a bark in the chow line, a line in the debrief, the brass being slower to trust him (rank, ADR-018). It is Platoon, and it costs him nothing but what it should cost him.
   KEEP IT LIGHT AND KEEP IT QUIET. No meter, ever (ADR-019 s4 governs here too). If it becomes a reputation bar, it dies.

DEPENDS ON: LW-2 (the ledger the tokens live in). Doors are worthless until the enemy inside them is smart (THE THINKING ENEMY - pwu5/0623/gpvb).

title: LW-8 THE AUTHORED THRESHOLD: the first walk out the wire (build LAST)
description:
ADR-020. Summoner: "its also key that the first time the players step out the wire there has to be some cool things that happen 'scripted' that will make them want to come back and see what else is going on out beyond the wire."

THE GOVERNING LAW: A RAIL TAKES THE CONTROLS AWAY. A GUARANTEE DOES NOT.

The first patrol is NOT scripted. It is AUTHORED-DENSE: the same procedural generator, run with a WEIGHTING PASS that GUARANTEES a set of encounters within ~400m of the wire. Nobody takes the stick. Nothing forces an outcome. The player is merely PROMISED that walking out that gate is the most interesting twenty minutes he has had.

(In a purely random world the first patrol can be forty minutes of empty green. THAT IS HOW YOU LOSE A PLAYER FOREVER. The guarantee exists to prevent that and for no other reason.)

THE GUARANTEE - each beat teaches a system by being LIVED, never by a tutorial popup. Placement procedural; existence guaranteed. EVERY ONE REFUSABLE:
- fresh trail sign, the point man stops and calls it   -> your point man is your eyes, listen to him
- a trip wire he catches BEFORE you walk into it       -> the jungle kills you, and this man just saved your life
- a VC patrol you can sit still and let walk past      -> contact is optional, and the +25 is real (ADR-006)
- a villager who is a person, not a target             -> the people are the war (ADR-019)
- a burned hut, a rotting ARVN body                    -> this war was here before you
- a firefight you HEAR (and may choose to walk toward) -> the war is bigger than you
- one gorgeous thing: a squall rolling in, Hueys crossing the treeline -> come back out here

Walk past the trail sign. Shoot the patrol instead of letting it pass. Ignore all of it. THE PLAYER MAY FAIL, SKIP, OR SPOIL ANY BEAT AND THE GAME SAYS NOTHING.

SET-PIECES ARE WORLD EVENTS, NEVER PLAYER EVENTS. Willard does not fly the Ride of the Valkyries - he WATCHES it from a boat.
BINDING TEST for every proposed set-piece: CAN THE PLAYER TURN AROUND AND LEAVE, RIGHT NOW, WITHOUT THE GAME STOPPING HIM OR PUNISHING HIM? If no, it is a RAIL, and it is FORBIDDEN.
(Note the test is CAN HE LEAVE - not "can he reach." Reachable battles he can join are LW-9 and they are correct.)

THE INTEREST CURVE IS FRONT-LOADED ON PURPOSE. Hour one is dense, loud, spectacular. Hour twenty is quiet - and by then the quiet is EARNED: it is DREAD, not boredom, because he now knows what is out there. WE BUY THE RIGHT TO BE BORING LATER BY BEING EXTRAORDINARY FIRST. This is what reconciles the threshold with the Ambience Law (LW-7) - they are the same curve read at two different times.

BUILD LAST: it is a weighting pass over finished systems and can only be tuned once they exist. It will constantly try to become a script. The Arbiter guards this and will lose the argument at least once.

title: LW-7 THE LIVING FIREBASE (under the Ambience Law - scarcity is the trick)
description:
ADR-020 s4. Summoner: "the firebase is the living home base that lives on its own 24/7 schedule of soldiers coming back from their own patrols, units waking up, going to eat food, guard shift switches, supply logistics coming in and dropping stuff off. and than sometimes a vc suicide attack, or a night raid by the enemy. you can be there or not but these things happen."

THE DEVIL'S ADVOCATE OBJECTION, UPHELD: if all of that is always firing, we have built the EXACT Battlefield chaos the Summoner rejected in the rival game ("constant combat and chaos everywhere but you're not really the main character"). Willard and the Platoon recruit do not work because a lot is happening. They work because ALMOST NOTHING HAPPENS - and then something unbearable does.

THE AMBIENCE LAW (binding):
  The living world's job is to make the QUIET feel OCCUPIED, not to make the war feel BUSY.
  Every ambient event must be SAFE TO IGNORE. The moment ignoring something COSTS the player, it is not ambience - it is a MISSION, and it belongs on the board at HQ.

The firebase is 95% MUNDANE: the chow line, cards, a guard shift changing, a man cleaning his rifle, mail arriving on a slick, a patrol coming back in short a man. All of it ignorable, none of it demanding.

Then ONE NIGHT IN TWENTY HOURS the wire gets hit - and it is the thing he remembers for the rest of the campaign. SCARCITY IS THE ENTIRE TRICK. A firebase attacked every third night is a Battlefield map.

WARNING FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THIS: you will want the wire hit more often "because we built the system." NO. The system's value is in how RARELY it fires.

title: LW-6 RANK gates authority, never ability. Player stats KILLED.
description:
ADR-018. The Summoner's own question, answered: player stats KILLED, squad XP kept but SILENT, rank NEW.

1. PLAYER STATS: KILLED.
No progression may touch accuracy, recoil, sway, handling, health, or stamina. EVER. A player-accuracy stat is hit-point math, and Pillar 1 forbids it ("death comes from SITUATION"). It also makes the first ten hours feel bad in the worst available way: "my guy cannot shoot yet." Your aim is your aim, mission 1 to mission 100.
-> This DELETES the St/Ag/Al player pool spend from GAME_GUIDE 4.4. A real divergence from the RECON tabletop, named in ADR-018 as GAME_GUIDE 5 requires.

2. SQUAD XP: kept, but SILENT and BEHAVIORAL. Never a number.
A veteran point man STOPS AND HOLDS UP A FIST before the trip wire; a green one walks you into it. The pigman's suppression tightens. Doc reaches you faster and lives through it. Callouts go from late-and-vague to early-and-right.
THIS IS PILLAR 4'S TEETH. Losing a veteran only hurts if a free rookie is visibly, audibly, painfully WORSE at his job. (Today loss is costless - GAME_GUIDE 4.4 admits it.)

3. PLAYER RANK: NEW. Gates AUTHORITY, not ABILITY.
GATES: fire-support tier (your own 60mm + a smoke marker -> 105s -> fast movers, napalm -> Arc Light) | what you are trusted with (mission types unlock; a new man is not handed a village raid) | the armory and the ruck (better weapons ARRIVE WITH SUPPLY, not "level 5 grants M16") | cosmetics (helmet, gear, ruck - seen in the firebase, and on your own corpse)
NEVER GATES: accuracy, recoil, sway, handling, health, bleed-out time. Anything a bullet cares about.

THE LADDER LAW (binding, Devil's Advocate upheld): rank gates HOW BIG, never WHETHER. A hardcore-lethality game with zero fire support at rank 1 is not hardcore, it is miserable. Rank 1 has a radio, a smoke marker, and his own 60mm mortars. It is a ladder, never a wall.

ADR-011 STANDS UNAMENDED: rank sets the MENU; the RTO sets the ACCESS. Lose him and rank buys you nothing.

title: LW-4 Mission length is geography: objective count by type
description:
ADR-017 SS5. Amends GAME_GUIDE SS4.6's flat 2-4 objectives.

  PATROL       | window contains the firebase | walk out the wire      | 1-2 obj | 20-30 min
  VILLAGE RAID | a few klicks out             | ride or walk (his call) | 2-3 obj | 30-45 min
  AIR ASSAULT  | across the province          | Huey (the load mask)    | 3-4 obj | 45-60 min

Summoner: 'the average mission length should be between 20 to 60 minutes, but its really up to the player and how they play for that length.'

Mission length is NOT a dial we set. It falls out of how far the thing is and how much of it there is. The HQ board shows all of them; the player picks by what he's got the stomach for tonight.

title: M1956 harness: apply to every US soldier as it is built
description:
The M1956 LCE harness is authored ONCE in art_source/characters/locker/gear_armory.blend (collection WEBBING), with its Shrinkwrap modifiers left LIVE, and snapshotted to locker/webbing_m1956.blend.

RULE: every US soldier gets the harness via 'blender -b -P tools/fit_webbing.py -- <unit>'. Do NOT copy the mesh onto a unit by hand.

WHY LIVE SHRINKWRAP: fit_webbing retargets each Shrinkwrap to THAT unit's body, so the harness RE-CONFORMS to a different soldier (a slimmer man gets a tighter belt). Copying baked geometry would clip or float.

BINDING (Caleb's spec: 'attachments ride on the webbing just like the real world'):
 - straps (belt/suspenders/yoke/bandolier) take skin weights FROM THE BODY via Data Transfer, so they bend when he bends
 - riders (pouches/buckles/clips) take weights FROM THEIR HOST STRAP; flaps/snaps take weights from their POUCH
 - verified: 0.00mm rider drift across 1041 frames / 96 clips

DONE: us_base_v3, us_rto  (both PASS the gate)
TODO: every future US unit (medic, grunt variants). Pilots do NOT get it - they wear survival vests.

Budget: harness 692 tris, body 434 = 1126 total (MoH-Frontline class).
Colour: art_source/characters/textures/canvas_od.png, army OD #4E5A31.
close_reason: M1956 harness authored, fitted to us_base_v3 + us_rto, gate PASSES (0.00mm rider drift, 1041 frames). Rule recorded: every US soldier gets it via tools/fit_webbing.py.

title: AUDIT-E1 [P1]: engine is NOT using Jolt physics + project.godot on defaults
description: physics/3d/physics_engine unset -> Godot Physics. Jolt is built in since 4.4 and is 2-5x faster on ragdoll/character-heavy scenes - exactly this game (ragdolls, gibs, PhysicalBone sims, fireteam AI). Needs a re-tune pass on enemy step height/unstick after the swap. Also: scaling_3d/mode unset -> BILINEAR while paying a 0.77 render-scale cost (switch to FSR2/FSR1 - also gives free temporal AA); mesh_lod threshold_pixels=1.0 so the LODs generated on all 266 GLBs never engage (set 2.0-4.0); max_fps uncapped; debanding off. Occlusion culling only pays AFTER baking OccluderInstance3D on structures/ridgelines - jungle canopy is a terrible occluder. Measure each with tests/perf_probe.gd.
close_reason: SHIPPED: Jolt Physics on (verified live at runtime, not just in the file - it silently reverted TWICE from killed benchmark shells, watch for that). Also FSR1 upscaling (was bilinear), mesh LOD threshold 2.0 (LODs were generated on 266 meshes and never engaged), max_fps 120, debanding. The Jolt SPEED claim remains unmeasured - see RECONgame-twig.

title: Gear gib-donors RENDER on top of the live gear - every grunt wears 2 helmets, 2 rucks, 2 bandoliers
description:
Found 2026-07-12 while reviewing us_rto in Blender, confirmed in-engine.

ModelActor._apply_gib_rig_contract() hides gib donors BY NAME PREFIX: grunt_*,
head_frag_*, cap_*. That covers the BODY donors. It does NOT cover the GEAR
donors, which have no naming convention:

  helmet_camo_shell, helmet_bugjuice, bandolier, bando_mag0..2,
  ruck_bag, ruck_crossbar, ruck_rail_l, ruck_rail_r

These are viewport-hidden in the .blend (they are the pieces that FLY OFF when a
region pops). Blender hide does not survive glTF, and the exporter deliberately
unhides everything - so they arrive in Godot visible, and nothing hides them again.

Verified with a probe on the shipped model: us_grunt_v2 renders helmet_camo_shell
AND the welded-in helmet; us_grunt_v3 renders helmet_camo_shell AND
helmet_shell_worn, ruck_bag AND ruck_pack_worn, bandolier AND bandolier_worn.

SO: this is PRE-EXISTING and it is shipping in us_grunt_v2 today - co-located
duplicate gear, i.e. z-fighting/shimmer on every soldier's helmet, ruck and
bandolier at range. Candidate for one of the "two visual P0 root causes" (mhfv).

It gets worse on v3, where the duplicates are now purely redundant.

FIX OPTIONS
  a) give the gear donors a `gib_` prefix in the blends + exporters, and add that
     prefix to the hide rule. GibSystem spawns donors by name, so its tables move
     with them.
  b) carry the Blender hide flag into the GLB (a glTF extra, or a name suffix) so
     the engine stops guessing which meshes are donors from their names.
(b) is the honest fix: the naming convention IS the bug - it silently fails open,
and "fails open" here means "renders".

title: DECISION: ship us_grunt_v3 as the live grunt? Hurtbox shrinks 47% head / 64% torso
description:
us_grunt_v3 is built, verified and committed, but NOTHING SPAWNS IT YET. ally_base.gd
still defaults to us_grunt_v2 and squad_system.gd uses us_grunt_m60 for the Pig. The
gear-in-hurtbox bug (RECONgame-rs9m) is therefore FIXED IN THE ASSET but still LIVE
IN THE GAME.

Flipping it is a one-line change per reference + re-export of the 3 gun variants from
the v3 base. It is held back deliberately because it changes combat feel and that is
Caleb's call, not mine:

  HEAD  hull 0.0126 -> 0.0067 m3  (-47%, the helmet leaves the hurtbox)
  TORSO hull 0.0566 -> 0.0206 m3  (-64%, the ruck and bandolier leave it)

WHAT THAT MEANS AT THE TRIGGER: rounds that used to "hit" a man by clipping his
backpack or his helmet's outer shell now MISS. Enemies get harder to kill, most
noticeably from behind and at grazing angles. Every hitzone still sits <=0.06m off
its bone segment (probe_hitzone_fit), so the hulls hug the man - they have not
collapsed, they have stopped enclosing his luggage.

The contract in hitzone_builder.gd is explicit that this is the INTENDED behaviour
("the player could shoot a man's ANTENNA and hurt him"), so this is a bug fix, not a
rebalance. But it is a bug fix the player will feel.

TO SHIP:
  1. ally_base.gd:171 sprite_unit -> "us_grunt_v3"
  2. re-export us_grunt_m14/m60/m79 from us_base_v3.blend (same exporter, gun arg),
     or the Pig keeps a 64%-bigger torso than the rest of the squad
  3. gore_dummy.gd / hitzone_editor.gd reference units - update or leave as v2 refs
  4. playtest: enemy TTK from behind
close_reason: RATIFIED BY THE SUMMONER 2026-07-13: 'we need to update his base model to v3'. ally_base.gd sprite_unit us_grunt_v2 -> us_grunt_v3; gore_dummy.gd likewise. The helmet and the ruck leave the hurtbox (HEAD -47%, TORSO -64%) - a BUG FIX, not a nerf: you could shoot a man's BACKPACK and kill him. The bill is paid knowingly - enemies are harder to kill from behind and at grazing angles. probe_orphaned_art: 4 orphans -> 2.

title: PERCEPTION MODEL v1 (Summoner decree): muzzle-origin combat vision, 25m spot cone, 125m combat decay, body serves the muzzle
description: Summoner spec 2026-07-11 verbatim intent: (1) NPC model orientation while shooting keys off the MuzzlePoint - muzzle is the pointer, body aligns to it. (2) Combat-mode vision ORIGIN = muzzle point. (3) Calm/patrol spotting = forward cone ~25m long (angle tunable, propose ~100 deg total) from body facing - defines who can SPOT player/allies and who counts as a WITNESS for ADR-005 beacon stamping. (4) Combat vision reaches 125m but spot-confidence + accuracy decay hard past the 25m core (curve tunable). (5) LETHALITY IS NEVER PERCEPTION-GATED: a stray round at range that hits a vital zone still kills - decay lives in aim spread/target-confidence only (ADR-016 damage grammar untouched). Replaces/standardizes per-enemy alert_range + exposure_ramp fields into cone params on EnemyData. DEPENDS: vi32 muzzle sockets (vision origin needs a real muzzle), synergizes with 7ks projectiles (muzzle-spawned rounds) and pwu5 (witness definition = this cone). Named cost: rear/flank approaches become strong stealth tools - intended jungle feel; open-terrain blindness past 25m calm-range accepted for v1.

title: KEYSTONE: EnemySquad coordinator (the director's make-or-break AI)
description:
Council keystone #2 - the linchpin for smart enemies. There is NO enemy squad layer (grep focus_fire|overwatch|coordinat = 0). Individual brain is good; build ONE coordinator that ASSIGNS roles to the existing goal-scorer - no new movement/fire code. Group membership already exists via group_tag.
Order: (1) breadcrumb trail - standalone S win, last_known_target_pos is one Vector3, doc specs 3 crumbs so they search where you WENT. (2) EnemySquad node: shared target designation + vis/alert sharing (M) = instant focus-fire. (3) fire cohesion: hold-until-contact + opening volley (S). (10) bounding overwatch = R62 stub (L).
Keep the FSM - it's a utility scorer with hysteresis, the right bones. Combat lab validates all of it. See COUNCIL_REVIEW.md.

title: AI NORTH STAR: smart enemies (patrols, search, teamwork, fire cohesion)
description:
Caleb, 2026-07-08 - the make-or-break directive for the whole game:

'highly intelligent and smart enemies is what will make or break this game. they need patrol routes, a tough searching mechanism when you are evading them, teamwork and firing cohesion. the NVA were not militarily strong but made up in determination and tactics.'

State today (post FOV-blindness fix):
- PERCEPTION now works: FOV cone + close-sense bubble + idle sentry scan; alert tiers RELAXED/SUSPICIOUS/ALERT/COMBAT; NoiseBus hearing; last-known-position investigate.
- Cover: dynamic cover-point discovery + claim broker exist (R15) but need real tuning against the combat lab.
- Navmesh: enemies path around structures (NavBaker, this session).
- GAPS to build toward the vision:
  1. PATROL ROUTES - trail-following exists (R18) but bare EnemyBase.spawn_enemy has no route; the mission generator should assign routes + sentry posts with real facings.
  2. SEARCH when evading - after losing LOS, escalate a COORDINATED sweep of the last-known area (breadcrumbs, spread search, flush cover), not just walk to one point. This is 'the tough searching mechanism'.
  3. TEAMWORK - squad-level coordination: bounding overwatch (one moves while one covers - R62 exists as a stub), suppress-while-flank, don't all pick the same cover (claim broker helps), call out contacts.
  4. FIRE COHESION - volley/focus-fire a spotted target, not independent plinking; hold fire until the point man triggers; concentrate on the nearest threat.
  5. DETERMINATION - morale that does NOT break easily for NVA regulars (vs VC militia that does); press even when hurt (retreats_when_hurt=false for NVA, already set).
This is the tuning target for the combat lab. Everything else (art, missions) is scaffolding around whether the firefight feels like fighting thinking soldiers.
notes:
AI GOAL DOCTRINE SHIPPED 2026-07-10 (war-room council + Summoner rulings, decree at war_room/synthesis_ai_goals.md): facing fixed (one global-yaw owner), anim intent policy (aim/aim-walk/run, honest strafe L-R, 0.25-band deadband), contact-confidence debounce both brains (goals never read raw LOS), 1s reactive dwell + Class-A damage interrupts + rush-completes, cover leash RE-ANCHORS (the release loop was the ally cover obsession), crowding-cost dispersion (no corner piles), ALLY PERSONALITY SPECTRUM (courage x skill per man per playthrough: coward anchors+sprays, go-getter pushes, presence rally +0.25 within 6m), ENEMY MORALE (courage break ladder: Local Force routs/surrenders, NVA holds), FULL-REALISM FF + muzzle discipline both factions, cover-adjacent wave spawns. Suite 33 PASS / 0 FAIL.
THE HUNT SHIPPED 2026-07-12 (probe_hunt.tscn 13/13) - gap #2 'SEARCH when evading / the tough searching mechanism' is CLOSED.

EnemySquad gained begin_hunt/hunt_point/hunt_active/hunt_radius/reanchor_hunt/end_hunt. Sectored expanding net biased along the crumb heading; stable per-man wedges via an alternating fan (0,+32,-32,+64,-64 deg) that does NOT depend on squad size; ring grows 1.4 m/s x determination to a 70m cap. enemy_base: losing contact BEGINS the hunt, the 5-second INVESTIGATE amnesia is replaced by hunt_active(determination), _execute_alert walks MY WEDGE not the shared crumb, and corpse discovery RE-ANCHORS the net.

NEW TRAIT: EnemyData.determination (courage = does he break; determination = does he go home). farmer 0.25/41s, VC 0.45/54s, sapper 0.7/70s, NVA 0.9/84s.

REMAINING gaps on this bead: #1 PATROL ROUTES (spawn_enemy still has no route/sentry facings), #3 TEAMWORK (bounding overwatch, suppress-while-flank), #4 FIRE COHESION (hold-until-contact + opening volley). #5 DETERMINATION is now DONE.

AUDIO: ambience is a global 2D loop - make it positional + varied
description:
Caleb: 'theres a chirpping bird constantly... if we do birds we need a few different bird calls and they need to have a real kinda melody. the helicoptor whirl noise is great but keep it to the location of the heli model not just the player.'

VERIFIED:
- game_world.gd:191 and :206 create plain AudioStreamPlayer (NON-positional, global) for jungle_loop.wav and the night bed. That is the constant chirp: one looping sample, everywhere, forever, at the same volume.
- Rotor is ALREADY correct: insertion_ride.gd:79 AudioStreamPlayer3D, max_distance 300, unit_size 20, and heli.add_child(_rotor) at :88 parents it to the aircraft. So if the whirl seems player-locked, the culprit is elsewhere - suspect the MENU rotor ambience (main_menu) leaking into the world, or insertion_ride.gd:80-82 MUTATING the shared preloaded ROTOR_LOOP resource in place (loop_mode/loop_end), which spooky_gunship.gd:38 also load()s from the same resource cache.

DESIGN:
- AmbienceDirector: a small pool of AudioStreamPlayer3D emitters placed on a Poisson disc around the player, re-seated as you move. Each picks from a per-biome, per-time-of-day call bank.
- Bird calls as 3-5 note MOTIFS, not a single chirp: pick a motif, transpose it, randomise the gap (8-25s). Silence is the instrument. Wildlife goes quiet near enemies (R31 already specs this tension tell).
- Layer: insect bed (2D, quiet) + positional wildlife (3D) + distant war (2D) + weather.
- Bank: 4-6 bird motifs (day), cicada swell, frog chorus (night), gibbon whoop (rare), monkey alarm (proximity tell), water lap near rivers, bamboo creak in wind.
notes: PARTIAL 2026-07-09: real 1hr jungle bed wired (random offset per mission, gitignored dev asset - needs license-clear replacement for release). Wildlife ducks in rain (fast out, 14s hesitant fade back), RAIN weather now squalls, procedural rain_loop.wav. Positional emitter ring already existed. Remaining: license-clear bed + more variety per biome/time.

title: PLAYTEST: squad command controls gone
description:

Code inspection so far (NOT yet reproduced):

- SquadSystem IS in the tree: game_flow.gd:161 world.add_child(squad).
- squad_system.gd:74 _unhandled_input gates on GameManager.can_player_act() (only checks is_paused/is_in_menu) and director.is_ended(). Neither should block at the pad.

title: PROVEN: roll_offers() is not deterministic - types.shuffle() uses the global RNG
description:
EXECUTED PROOF, probe_smoke_all.gd section C:
  _roll_types(999) -> [3, 1, 0]
  _roll_types(999) -> [0, 1, 4]   (same rng seed!)

mission_select.gd:19 calls types.shuffle(), which draws from the GLOBAL RNG, despite roll_offers() receiving a seeded RandomNumberGenerator as a parameter. Also confirmed: pick_random() DOES honour seed(), so routing everything through a MissionRNG will work (Step 4).
close_reason: FIXED: mission_select.roll_offers() now uses manual Fisher-Yates with rng.randi(), not Array.shuffle() (global RNG).

title: PROVEN: R88 seed replay loads a different world than you played
description:
EXECUTED PROOF, probe_smoke_all.gd section C:
  roll_offers(rng seed 12345) -> offer.world_seed=39747, offer.mission_seed=76956
  debrief prints mission_seed (mission_state.gd:80 -> debrief.gd:59) = 76956
  offer_for_seed(76956) -> world_seed=76956   != 39747

mission_select.gd:21,26 draws world_seed and mission_seed as two INDEPENDENT rng.randi() calls; offer_for_seed (:41-44) sets both to the same value. Share-a-seed play (R88) gives your friend different terrain, different site placement, different objectives.

Fix: carry both seeds through the result dict and the replay row.
close_reason: FIXED: mission_select now sets world_seed = mission_seed (one seed = one op, R88 replay integrity).

title: PROVEN: any_fire_menu_open softlocks kit keys for the rest of the session
description:
EXECUTED PROOF, tests/probe_smoke_all.gd section B:
  d1 = MissionDirector.new(); d1.fire_menu_open = true; d1.free()
  d2 = MissionDirector.new()
  -> MissionDirector.any_fire_menu_open is STILL TRUE

mission_director.gd:171 static var any_fire_menu_open. The member 'var fire_menu_open: bool = false' has a setter, but GDScript does NOT invoke a setter for a member initializer, so a fresh director never clears the static.

Effect: die or exfil with the fire-support menu [T] open -> equipment_manager.gd:62 blocks ALL slot keys (1-4, wheel) and player.gd:528 blocks smoke, for the remainder of the process. Recover only by pressing T twice.

Fix in Step 3 MissionScope.reset().
close_reason: FIXED: MissionScope.reset() clears any_fire_menu_open static on teardown.

title: STEP-1: harness made trustworthy (DONE)
description:
1. run_all_tests.ps1 no longer does '2>&1 | Out-Null'. Output is captured and scanned line-by-line.
   - Verified empirically that Godot 4.6.2 emits 'ERROR: <msg>' for push_error, NOT 'SCRIPT ERROR' or 'USER ERROR'. The originally-planned patterns would never have fired - the exact bug class this harness exists to catch.
   - Verified that PowerShell -like treats '[NAV]' as a character class (matches any N/A/V) and matched every test. Switched to .Contains() ordinal matching.
   - Positive control: confirmed capture works by asserting 'Godot Engine' and a deliberate push_error text are both present in captured output.
2. Verdicts: PASS / LEAK (benign, loud, non-fatal) / FAIL / XFAIL / XPASS.
   - XPASS (a KnownRed test that starts passing) FAILS the build, forcing removal from the list.
   - LEAK is not a whitelist-to-silence: it prints per-test and in the summary, and points at AUDIT-12.
3. Test save isolation via '-- --test-save' (see AUDIT-13).
4. tests/test_nav_path.gd + .tscn added, registered KNOWN-RED. It reports:
     'regions on map: 25 | path points: 0'
   25 empty NavigationRegion3D are registered to the nav map and contribute zero polygons. Assertions 1-3 (navmesh exists / hut is carved / detour is real) are live; Assertion 4 (drive a real EnemyBase around the hut) lands with NavBaker in Step 6.
5. Bonus fixes found while in campaign_state.gd:
   - reset_campaign() cleared iron_man (the wipe disabled the mode that caused it) - now preserved.
   - reset_campaign() never cleared intel_points - now does.
   - load_campaign() returned silently on ANY error; now distinguishes ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND (normal first boot) from a corrupt/unreadable file (push_error).
   - save_campaign() ignored ConfigFile.save()'s return; now push_errors.
close_reason: SHIPPED: run_all_tests.ps1 captures+scans output line-by-line (ordinal .Contains, not -like); PASS/LEAK/FAIL/XFAIL/XPASS verdicts; XPASS fails build; save isolation via --test-save. Harness is trustworthy.

title: AUDIT-13: test suite wrote to the player's real user://campaign.cfg
description:
FIXED in Step 1 (this issue is the record).

reset_campaign() is called by FIVE test files - test_campaign_state:11, test_xp_spend:11,61, test_squad:10,131, test_firebase_sim:52, test_huey_ride:22,112 - and test_full_loop instantiates the real main.tscn GameFlow and runs three missions to debrief, firing game_flow.gd:190 CampaignState.on_mission_end() -> save_campaign().

run_all_tests.ps1 launches godot --headless --path $root, i.e. the same project and the same user:// directory. Running the suite once wiped the player's roster, XP, threat level, mission log and Iron Man flag, then overwrote the file with test garbage.

Fix: CampaignState.is_test_run() checks OS.get_cmdline_user_args() for '--test-save'; run_all_tests.ps1 now passes it. save_path resolves to user://campaign_test.cfg, deleted at _ready() so each run starts clean. Verified: user://campaign.cfg mtime unchanged across a full suite run.
close_reason: Step 1: test save isolation via --test-save -> campaign_test.cfg.

title: AUDIT-01: Barracks can only ever sell the player 'small_arms'
description:
campaign_state.gd:17 hardcodes player_data.mos='RIFLEMAN'. barracks.gd:60 derives ONE purchasable skill from MOS via SkillCatalog.MOS_SKILL. MOS_SKILL['RIFLEMAN']='small_arms'. So the player can never buy fo_fac, demolitions, silent_movement, medic, detect_ambush, sniping.

Consequence: 4 of the 6 player_skill() read sites are structurally pinned to 0 forever -
  mission_director.gd:196  player_skill('fo_fac')        -> CAS turnaround never improves
  mission_generator.gd:352 player_skill('demolitions')   -> plant speed never improves
  plant_charge.gd:28       player_skill('demolitions')   -> player never spots trap wires
  player.gd:426            player_skill('silent_movement') -> footstep radius never shrinks

Also: 'detect_ambush' is buyable by POINT but read NOWHERE (squad_system.gd:181 uses raw 'al'). 'sniping' (skill_catalog.gd:13) is neither buyable nor read - pure fiction.
Only medic is cross-wired correctly (squad_system.gd:151 reads the medic's own member dict).

WAVE3_REPORT.md:17 and PLAYER_MANUAL.md:32 both claim 'every purchase does something real'. False.
Fix: let the player buy from the full catalog, or route ally skill purchases into the systems that read them.
close_reason: Step 7: Barracks 2+4 split. Player buys small_arms/sniping/silent_movement; RTO/GRENADIER/POINT/MEDIC own their role skills, read via roster_skill/member_by_mos. test_skills green.

Promote-on-death/disengage reassignment, owned by the EnemySquad coordinator (single targeting authority). GUARD-RAIL: witness heartbeat (perception+NoiseBus) + persistent state tick on EVERY tier at EVERY distance; never set_physics_process(false) to shed AI cost (would void ADR-005 loud-kill beacon). Profile hot-set size on a REAL mission (bench 40ms is contaminated by O(18x18) patrol LOS + debug ImmediateMesh + telemetry walks). Measured 2026-07-16: after cheap GPU fixes the frame is CPU-bound at ~41ms - THIS is the wall.

title: Radio handset tether: grab from RTO, cord to player's hand, fire-mission leash
description:
Caleb's design: 'the player goes up to the radio man, gets the radio from him and then its tethered to the radio man by a cord so you have to stick close to them. and thats how you call in fire missions'

BUILT (scripts, not yet wired into a scene):
 - scripts/gameplay/radio_cord.gd    (RadioCord, ImmediateMesh)
 - scripts/gameplay/radio_handset.gd (RadioHandset, STOWED/HELD swap)

THE CORD IS PROCEDURAL, ALWAYS. No static cord mesh - one system draws it whether the
handset is clipped to the RTO or stretched to the player, so the two cases cannot
disagree. It routes through THREE points:
    CordPort (Spine2) -> CordGuide (LeftShoulder) -> handset boss
The shoulder guide is load-bearing: a straight line from a radio on his BACK to a hand
in FRONT of him passes through his chest. All three markers are bone-attached, so the
routing survives him turning, walking and dying.

SAG = TENSION READOUT. Slack becomes belly. The cord droops when the player is close and
straightens as he runs out of leash. No UI needed - he can SEE his leash.

THE LEASH DOES NOT BLOCK MOVEMENT (deliberate):
  0-75%   free
  75-100% taut, cord straightens, cord_taut signal fires once
  >100%   handset RIPPED from his hand, snaps back to the RTO (cord_snapped)
A hard movement block in an FPS = walking into an invisible wall while being shot at.
Player is never trapped; he just loses the call.

HOLDING IT COSTS THE RIFLE - handset_taken is emitted so the weapon system stows the
weapon. That is what makes calling artillery a DECISION, and what makes the
'call the RTO over and have him hunker' command matter (see the shelved radio design).

title: Viewmodel: real second-camera lens (transparent SubViewport)
description: The shipped viewmodel_fov scales the gun by the lens ratio in the shared camera - a close approximation. The textbook version renders the viewmodel through its own Camera3D in a transparent SubViewport composited over the world. Written and proven once (the framing was perfect) but the world went BLACK behind it: with own_world_3d, the project's default environment paints an opaque backdrop into the subviewport, and transparent_bg did not clear it. FIX TO TRY: assign an explicit Environment to the subviewport's World3D with background_mode = BG_CLEAR_COLOR and a zero-alpha clear colour (or BG_CANVAS), and verify with tools/screenshot_runner on gun_range - the range floor MUST be visible behind the rifle. Two payoffs when it lands: the gun can never clip into world geometry, and world FOV becomes a player graphics setting without every weapon changing size.

title: CIVILIAN THREAT RESPONSE: what triggers hands_up vs cower vs flee (Caleb's question)
description:
Caleb, 2026-07-12, while posing civ_hands_up: "why are they putting their hands up? do
they do that when the player is too close with their gun?"

Yes - and the trigger is what gives the moment meaning. It splits into three, and each
clip answers a DIFFERENT question the player is asking:

  HANDS UP   = A WEAPON IS AIMED AT ME.
               Player within ~15m, line of sight, and AIMING - the muzzle is on him.
               A DIRECTED threat. He freezes, hands up, and SHAKES HIS HEAD.
               The head shake is doing real work: it is a NEGATION. He is TALKING to
               you - "no, I am not VC, do not shoot". It tells the player this one is
               communicating, not reaching for something. That is the humanising beat
               and it is exactly what makes the decision hard.

  COWER      = THERE IS SHOOTING HAPPENING.
               Not at him - a firefight nearby, rounds cracking overhead. AMBIENT
               violence. He drops and protects his skull. Nobody is pointing anything
               at him; he just wants to be small.

  FLEE       = IT IS CLOSE AND I CAN GET OUT.
               Same trigger as the cower, but he has somewhere to run. civ_panic_run.

CLIPS EXIST (workbench): civ_hands_up + civ_hands_up_raise (one-shot), civ_cower,
civ_panic_run. Built on Caleb's poses.

THE THING THIS WHOLE SYSTEM IS FOR - DESIGN CALL, NOT MINE:
A VC CAN FAKE IT. A guerrilla in black pyjamas with his hands up is indistinguishable
from a farmer with his hands up - we built them on the same base, from the same locker,
in the same clothes. Some of them drop their hands and shoot when you turn your back or
walk past. That is the actual war, and it is the best possible use of the civilians.
It also has to be handled carefully: it can read as a cheap gotcha if every third
farmer is a trap. Suggest it is RARE, and that there are TELLS (he does not shake his
head; he watches your muzzle instead of your face; he is standing where a farmer would
not stand).

CONSEQUENCES (pillars: "escalation not fail-states", "fail forward"): shooting a
civilian must NOT be a fail state. It should cost - village hostility, VC recruitment,
RECON score penalty (RECON RPG has scoring for this) - and the mission continues.

title: RUNTIME CHARACTER COMPOSITION: stop baking every variant into its own GLB
description:
Caleb's idea, 2026-07-12, and it is the right destination. We are currently doing the
PRE-COMPOSED version of character variety: every combination is baked into its own
GLB. civ_farmer_m_b is an entire separate character file just because he is brown and
holds a sickle. Ten civilian GLBs already, and it is combinatorial - 3 shirt colours x
4 props x 2 hats = 24 files, and it only gets worse when the VC want the same props.

HOW THE INDUSTRY SPLITS IT (three INDEPENDENT axes; the mistake is fusing them):

  1. ATTACHMENTS - rigid props on a socket. Weapons, helmets, radios, a sickle.
     Parented to a bone, no deformation. Godot: BoneAttachment3D.
     *** WE ALREADY HAVE THIS. *** The locker is exactly it: 16 pieces, each
     declaring its bone, each gear-named so the hitzone harvester skips it. Rides
     any model on the standard rig, contributes zero hitbox. Proven in-engine.

  2. MODULAR SKINNED PARTS - clothing that DEFORMS. The body is authored as swappable
     SKINNED chunks (torso / legs / arms / head), all bound to the SAME skeleton, so
     a picked set deforms as one mesh. Destiny, The Division, Fallout 4, Warframe.
     A hat is an attachment; a SHIRT is a modular part, because it has to bend when
     he bends. WE DO NOT HAVE THIS - our shirt is baked into the body, which is why
     ba-ba pyjamas had to be made by RESHAPING the grunt's body instead of swapping
     a shirt onto him.

  3. MATERIAL VARIATION - tint masks. One texture plus an RGB mask marking
     shirt/trousers/trim, three tint colours fed per-instance. Free variety, no new
     meshes. Ours are baked into separate textures = the expensive way.

THE COMPOSITION STEP: a loadout data asset - body set + head + tint + attachment list
- rolled from a SEED at spawn. Seeded so it is deterministic (and would replicate
identically across clients if this ever goes multiplayer).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING (it is small):
  * ModelActor.attach(piece_name, bone) - load a gear GLB, hang it on a
    BoneAttachment3D. make_gear_library ALREADY exports each piece as its own GLB
    into assets/models/gear/, so the assets exist today.
  * a CivilianLoadout / UnitLoadout resource + a seeded roll at spawn
  * (later, bigger) tint-mask materials to kill the baked colour variants
  * (later, biggest) modular skinned torso/legs so clothing is swappable, not carved

DO NOT START THIS MID-ART-PASS. It is an engine change and the models are still being
finished. But nothing we have built is in its way: the bone-attached, unskinned,
gear-named contract IS the foundation this system needs, and it is already load-bearing.

title: Soft-cover penetration: concealment is not cover (brush/thatch/bamboo)
description: Caleb's 00 buck research: 9 pellets, 0.33in each (9mm-class), 'great power for punching through thick jungle brush'. Confirmed our pattern already matches 9 pellets. Implemented the brush property: world geometry in group 'soft_cover' (site_planner tags hooch/hut/thatch/bamboo/fence/shack/crate by name) is PUNCHED THROUGH by rounds - 2 layers, 20% energy each - while bunkers/rock/vehicles still stop lead. Applies to BulletSystem rounds and to every shotgun pellet independently (nine balls each punching their own way = the historical reason a point man carried a 12-gauge). Foliage/grass already had no colliders (concealment by design). Probe tools/probe_brush.tscn: M16 through thatch = 64 dmg, into a bunker = 0. Note for the P3 bead: this is the cheap 80% of material penetration; real thickness/material tables are still open.

title: ADR-016 Amendment F: explosives kill (M26 190, RPG 250/290, LAW 250, M79 150)
description: Summoner decree. Rockets now outclass grenades. Also killed a data lie: grenade.gd hardcoded 130/25/8m while m26_grenade.tres said 55 - grenade.gd now READS the tres (one number, one law), radius 10m, rim 13% of centre. title: FIRE MISSION via tethered PRC-25 handset (design locked, NOT started)
description:
Caleb's design, refined 2026-07-12. SHELVED - do not start without his go-ahead.

THE LOOP
  1. Squad command "RTO, ON ME". He breaks off, moves to the player, and hunkers in
     the nearest cover within cord reach (prone in the open if there is none - the
     game does not rescue the player from a bad hole).
  2. Once he is set: prompt to take the handset. Rifle goes SLUNG - you cannot shoot
     while you are on the horn.
  3. Cord tether ~4m (the real PRC-25 cord is ~1.8m; 4m for playability). Step past
     it and the handset is ripped from your hand: call aborted, short cooldown.
     NEVER a movement lock - taking the player's controls away feels awful.
  4. Call takes real time (grid, adjust, splash). Both of you static, next to a
     kneeling man with a metre of steel antenna over his head.
  5. "RTO, REJOIN" releases him. He does NOT stand up on his own the moment the call
     ends - or he stands into the counter-battery you just called on yourself.

WHY "CALL HIM TO ME" AND NOT "POSITION HIM":
the radio does not need line of sight. The PLAYER is the forward observer. Asking
the player to position the RTO for a vantage was a FAKE decision. The real one is
WHERE DO I CALL FROM and WHEN DO I SUMMON HIM.

WHAT KEEPS IT FROM BEING TRIVIALLY SAFE: he has to WALK to you. 40m back = ~15s of a
man crossing open ground with an antenna up. Summon him early and you have committed
him to your position; summon him late and he runs through fire to reach you.
Suppression slows him - under heavy fire he goes to ground and crawls. If he dies,
it is because you called late: a real mistake, not a frustrating one.

FAIL FORWARD
  * RTO dies -> cord goes slack, handset dead. You can pull the PRC-25 off his body
    and carry it yourself - then YOU are the man with the antenna and you take the
    aggro.
  * The radio is a separate mesh OUTSIDE the hurtbox (v3 gear contract), so it can
    carry its own small destructible collider. Shoot the radio: no fire missions for
    the rest of the mission. Escalation, not a fail state.

ENEMY AI HOOK: a man with an antenna is a priority target (historically true). Ties
into the EnemySquad coordinator (gpvb).

FIRST SLICE WHEN GREENLIT: FP handset viewmodel (of80) + the on-me/hunker behaviour.
Fire-mission UI and the destructible radio after. Assets already exist: prc25_handset,
prc25_cord, prc25_radio_pack, prc25_antenna (gear_library.blend), and us_rto.

title: RPG fuze arming + rockets were TUNNELLING through everything
description: Caleb asked for Arma-style arming distance. Research (PG-2/B-40, the Vietnam launcher we ship): drop-safe piezoelectric impact fuze that arms only after launch and a short travel via setback acceleration; PG-7 arms at 3-15m with an inertial base switch closing at booster burnout, and self-destructs at 3.8-6s. Implemented: ProjectileData.arming_distance (PG-2 = 5m), dud_impact_frac (unarmed strike = kinetic only, 20% dmg, no blast), self_destruct (armed rounds detonate at end of run; duds never blow). BIGGER BUG FOUND: ProjectileBase moved by teleporting global_position and relied on Area3D OVERLAP - at 84 m/s that is 1.4m per tick, so rockets TUNNELLED through walls, men and hitzones and expired downrange having touched nothing. This is why the RPG never exploded on anything. Now segment-raycasts each step like BulletSystem, excluding the shooter and his own hitzones. Probe: tools/probe_fuze.tscn (drop-safe at 3m, 62 blast dmg at 30m). NOTE for ADR-016: an armed PG-2 detonating 1.2m from a 70hp man leaves him alive (base 62) - anti-tank rocket, anti-personnel result. Worth a lethality decision.
close_reason: SHIPPED: PG-2 arming distance 5m (drop-safe - a rocket at your feet is a clang, not a crater), self-destruct at end of run, warhead leaves the tube on fire. AND the root cause it exposed: rockets were TUNNELLING through walls/men/hitzones (Area overlap at 1.4m per tick) - they now segment-raycast like bullets. Rockets had never reliably hit anything.

title: RPG fixed: parabola, no explosion, warhead stays in tube
description: Caleb range test. (1) ARC: the sight-zero elevation was applied to the AIM RAY, so on an 84 m/s rocket with a 200m default zero the aim point sat 8deg up - 3.5m over a man 25m away - and the rocket was thrown at it. Aim ray is now the pure crosshair; elevation belongs to the launch. Rockets get a LAUNCHER sight: elevate for the ACTUAL distance to the aim point using the projectile's OWN gravity_scale (0.12) and speed - point at a man 25m out, the rocket goes into him. Enemy RPG gunners had the same 8x over-elevation; fixed. (2) NO EXPLOSION: a projectile that reached its lifetime _expire()d silently - a rocket that sailed over a man simply blinked out. Warheads now self-destruct (AOE) at end of run, as real RPG rounds do. (3) WARHEAD IN TUBE: the RPG viewmodel is one mesh but the warhead is its own surface (material 'WarheadOD'), so it is hidden on fire and restored on reload - generic: any launcher whose warhead material name contains 'warhead' gets it free. Blender nicety later: split the warhead into its own object for a proper fly-out.
close_reason: Superseded/completed by the fuze work: arc, explosion, warhead and the tunnelling root cause all shipped.

title: Hitzone coverage: seams closed (12.9% of frontal hits registered NOTHING)
description: Research + measurement answer to Caleb's 'can we just bake collision into the model' question. Industry: nobody uses render-mesh per-poly on animated characters - CS2 moved boxes->capsules, Arma uses a Fire Geometry LOD of convex components with named selections. Godot: mesh->collision gives a STATIC snapshot (ConcavePolygonShape3D cannot ride a skeleton and is barred from moving bodies); the only live options are per-bone primitives or our approach (convex hulls cut from the real mesh, synced to bones) = Arma-tier. tools/probe_hitbox_coverage.gd bakes the skinned render mesh as a trimesh and fires a 1.2cm ray grid: with zero margin, 12.9% of frontal rays that hit the grunt's BODY hit NO zone (22.3% VC) - bullets slipping through the concave wedges (armpit, hip, shoulder) that no convex hull owns. That was 'I hit him and nothing happened'. Fixed: DEFAULT_INFLATE 3cm -> grunt 96.7% front / 100% side. VC residual (10%) is the 8-loose-parts body - Blender join (VC_FIX_LIST) closes it. Suite guards updated (BODY-hull check now guards the human window, not a bone-span capsule).
close_reason: SUPERSEDED and properly fixed: the 3cm seam margin was a band-aid (Caleb called it: the VC body join changed coverage by ZERO). Real cause was structural - convex hulls butting at joints. Fixed by INTERLOCK (joint bones harvest into both neighbouring regions). 100% coverage front+side on both rigs, with a third LESS overhang, margin down to 1cm.

title: Grunt body has GEAR WELDED INTO the joined mesh - it lands in the hurtbox
description:
FOUND 2026-07-12 while building the gear library. us_grunt_joined is not just a body: its 15 materials include MitchellCamo (helmet camo), Webbing, BandolierCloth, Fatigue + AluFrame (ruck), and even weapon mats. Bounds prove it: z reaches 1.822 (head top is 1.74 -> helmet baked in) and y reaches 0.247 (ruck volume); 186 verts sit above head-top, 42 in the ruck volume.

TWO CONSEQUENCES:
1. HURTBOX: HitzoneBuilder excludes gear BY MESH NAME (_GEAR_NAME_HINTS). 'us_grunt_joined' is not a gear name, so the helmet and ruck geometry ARE harvested into the hitzone hulls - the head zone is inflated by the helmet and the torso zone by the ruck. The 'gear never enters the hurtbox' contract is silently broken for the grunt.
2. MODULARITY: gear cannot be swapped or removed per-variant. You cannot make an RTO by hiding the ruck, because the ruck IS the body. This blocks the whole modular-kit direction (Summoner approved 2026-07-12: gear separate, placed over models).

Also note the separate helmet_camo_shell (153 verts) DUPLICATES the baked helmet, and separate ruck_bag is an 8-vert stub.

FIX: cut the gear geometry out of us_grunt_joined into bone-parented meshes named with gear hint words (the gear_library.blend pattern), leaving the joined mesh as BODY ONLY. Then re-export and re-verify: probe_silhouette (parts=1), test_gore_rig, and a hitzone check that the head hull no longer includes the helmet. RISK: touches the truth source every unit derives from - do it deliberately, with the probes green before and after.
close_reason:
FIXED + VERIFIED. tools/make_base_v3.py clones us_grunt_v2.blend -> us_base_v3.blend
(truth source untouched) and cuts the welded-in gear into rigid BONE-PARENTED meshes:
helmet_shell_worn(Head), bandolier_worn+ruck_pack_worn(Spine2), pouch_belt_worn(Hips).

Hurtbox proof (tools/probe_hurtbox_size.gd, new):
  HEAD   0.0126 -> 0.0067 m3  (-47%, helmet out)
  TORSO  0.0566 -> 0.0206 m3  (-64%, ruck+bandolier out)
  every zone still <=0.06m off its bone segment (probe_hitzone_fit: no floaters)
Skeleton unchanged: rest-span 1.69, k=1.016, gib_scale=0.49, parts=1.
In-engine: all 4 import as BoneAttachment3D; helmet tracks the head bone 1:1.

Gotcha for the next unit: a belt pouch was modelled with the BODY's material, so a
material-only cut misses it. Pass 2 catches it as a tiny DETACHED island - and must
run AFTER the material strip, or the gear itself reads as islands.

Also fixed in export_us_grunt_v2.py: body_bbox() must include the *_worn gear.
TARGET_HEIGHT is to the HELMET TOP; measuring the body alone put his bare skull at
1.7132m and silently grew every grunt by a helmet's height.

Commit 7871eb4 on overnight-claude.

CORE VIETNAM FIREBASE TACTIC (the authenticity hook):
- Sited to control a CHOKEPOINT: a road junction or a high point/hilltop.
- ALL vegetation around it is blasted/cleared - fields of fire. Use ClearingSystem to strip trees in a radius; the result is bare RED CLAY, dusty, denuded hillside.
- Reuse the TREE STUMP billboards on the cleared slopes to sell 'we cut this hill bald' - and the SAME stumps work for post-napalm / post-arclight scars.
- Red clay dust ground texture / decal in the cleared ring (distinct from jungle floor).

This is a SitePlanner + terrain-material + ClearingSystem job, mostly using assets/systems that already exist. High authenticity-per-effort.

title: PERF: steady-state is 19-25 FPS on Intel UHD, not the 35.6 in WAVE3_REPORT
description:
MEASURED, tests/probe_perf_decay.gd, windowed, real renderer, GameWorld seed 4242, player idle, 56s:

  t=4s..52s   fps 19-25, nodes 716 (flat), orphans 0, objects 210, draws 104,
              prims 295497, mem 304.1MB, vram 187.3MB, chunks 25 -- ALL FLAT.

Two hypotheses I formed from the MCP debug log and then REFUTED by measurement:
1. 'FPS decays monotonically 39->14' - FALSE. That was the world finishing its
   billboard queue (1/frame); early samples were fast because less was drawn.
   Steady state is flat. No leak: zero orphan growth over 56s.
2. 'Chunks are thrashing (chunk (1,4) billboards generated 5x)' - FALSE. A clean
   run logs exactly 25 mesh builds, 25 vegetation materialize, 25 billboard gens.
   The duplicate lines were an MCP output-buffer artifact.

What IS true: the game sits at ~20 FPS at spawn on the target GPU. WAVE3_REPORT.md
claims 35.6 avg and ROADMAP_NEXT claims min 19. Reconcile the number or the claim.
Budget this before the bush-density work (see the bush epic).
notes: AUDIT (tech director): likely renderer-level - project.godot never sets rendering_method (Forward+ on Intel UHD, only 104 draws/295k prims). Perf-spike day checklist: test rendering_method=mobile, de-light muzzle flashes (OmniLight3D per flash gun_fx.gd:117), FIFO-cap scar decals past deform ceiling (damage_system.gd:143-191), unshade clutter, add AI frame budget (MAX_THINK_TIME declared never used enemy_base.gd:173). Measure before/after.
close_reason: RETIRED: its 19-25 FPS figure is VOID - measured at 0.77 render scale (59% native pixels) like every prior number. No honest FPS number exists until 365s reprofiles at native. Superseded by 365s.

title: [epic] CAPTURE: downed -> POW -> escape / bribe / rescue / suicide / wait-it-out
description:
Caleb's design, 2026-07-08. The strongest idea in the batch. It converts 'you died, reload' into 'the campaign continues without you, and you are somewhere else.' That IS Pillar 5 (fail forward), taken further than the medic chain.

CAPTURE TRIGGER (elegant, and mostly already built):
- You go DOWN, not dead. health_system.gd already has the downed state + bleed timer + squad revive chain (squad_system.gd:117-160).
- An enemy stands over you for ~5s -> CAPTURED.
- Caleb's key insight: your whole team need NOT be dead. They just have to fail to reach you while a man is standing on you. The 5s window is the drama. A squadmate can shoot him off you.
- This makes the existing revive chain a RACE, not a formality.

OUTCOMES (POW camp):
1. ESCAPE - break out. RESCUE mission type already has a camp, cage and guards (W48) - invert it, you are in the cage.
2. BRIBE - buy your way out. NEEDS THE MONEY ECONOMY (see the RPG loop epic).
3. RESCUED - another RECON squad comes for you. Scripted to start, then LIVE gameplay: the rescue team can LOSE. Deliciously grim.
4. SUICIDE - end it yourself. Deer Hunter russian roulette scene requested.
5. WAIT IT OUT - the war ends around you. THIS IS AN ENDING. A real one.

CONTENT WARNING / DESIGN GATE: russian roulette, suicide-as-mechanic, and (from the Battle Director epic) a child suicide bomber are three separate hard-content decisions. They can be done with restraint and enormous power, or they can be edgelord garbage. This needs a War Room with the writer and the devil's advocate BEFORE any of it is implemented. Do not let it arrive by accident inside a feature commit.

REUSE - VERIFIED: C:/Users/caleb/CatacombsOfGore (project name 'Broken Provinces') has scripts/autoload/bounty_manager.gd, data/bounty_templates*.json, and data/items/jail_key.tres. That is a BOUNTY/reputation system with a jail, not a capture state machine - the reusable part is the bounty/faction-standing model and the jail-key/escape scaffolding, not a drop-in POW system. Read it before assuming.

DEPENDS ON: Step 5 save integrity (a capture must survive a quit; today save_campaign() fires mid-mission and would persist a half-state - squad_system.gd:246-251).

title: [epic] RIDE OR WALK: player-chosen approach, with a patrol-density consequence
description:
Caleb's design, 2026-07-08: 'the player can choose to ride a vehicle on land to the objective, or just walk it... if they walk out of the gate it says something like "looks like were huffing it" and it will initially keep the patrols down until the first contact.'

Why this is good: it makes Pillar 3 (freedom, no rails) a MECHANICAL choice with a real tradeoff, not a flavour one. Vehicle = fast, loud, road-bound, ambushable, mines. Foot = slow, quiet, off-road, and the AO starts cold.

MECHANIC: an approach modifier on MissionDirector's escalation pool.
- FOOT: patrol density x0.5 until first contact, then it normalises (the hunter escalation from CONTENT+COMBAT WAVE already models 'after first blood').
- VEHICLE: full density from t=0, but you arrive with time and stamina banked; road-bound so the ambush deck (RealVietnamRTS ambush_manager.gd) gets its moment.

ASSETS: M35 truck + M113 GLBs already imported (NS05). destructible_vehicle.gd already exists. Drivable is rework, not new.
NOTE: 'looks like we're huffing it' is exactly the right register. Squad barks carry this, not a UI toast.

DEPENDS ON: Step 6 navmesh (a vehicle needs a road network to follow, and R33 trail rendering is still unbuilt - only the patrol half of R33 shipped).

title: [epic] BATTLE DIRECTOR: campaign-reactive dynamic events
description:
Caleb's design, 2026-07-08. RTS-style director for the campaign layer, not just the tactical one.

CORE: the campaign already has the state a director needs - CampaignState.threat_level w/ decaying modifiers, team_xp, roster, intel_points, mission_log, missions_played. Today it only nudges AA density. Make it drive EVENTS.

Shape: after each debrief, the director rolls against campaign state and may inject a mutation into the NEXT departure:
- FIREBASE ASSAULT: you were doing well -> the AO answers. Big wave hits the firebase before you deploy. (FIREBASE_DEFENSE already exists as a mission type - reuse it as an EVENT, not an offer.)
- TERROR ATTACK: a sapper/child suicide bomber inside the wire. Deliberately ugly. Needs a hard content conversation before it ships.
- AMBUSHED CONVOY / MEDEVAC / DOWNED PILOT nearby -> a divert.
- QUIET WEEK: nothing. The director must be allowed to do nothing, or every return-to-base becomes a cutscene.

PRESSURE VALVE: this is where the RPG loop lands (see the money/shop epic). Success raises heat; heat raises event odds; events cost you men and materiel; you spend XP+money to recover. That is the loop.

DEPENDS ON: Step 4 determinism (a director rolling on the global RNG cannot be tested, replayed, or bisected). Do NOT build this before MissionRNG.
DEPENDS ON: Step 3 MissionScope (events fire across mission boundaries; static leakage will make them behave differently on mission 5 than mission 1).

The RTS project's ai_director.gd (RealVietnamRTS battle_system/ai/) is the design seed - encounter pacing + doctrine. Read it before writing this.

title: stamp_firebase() ignores its rng - every firebase is identical
description:
Godot's own compiler: 'WARNING: The parameter "rng" is never used in the function "stamp_firebase()"' (site_planner.gd:169). The function iterates the const SiteLayouts.FIREBASE_INTERIOR array; MG nests are placed at fixed north/south points. Every firebase on every seed in every mission has an identical interior layout.

NOTE: probe_smoke_all.gd's firebase check reported OK. That check is INVALID - it compares 'node.name@x,z' strings, and Godot uniquifies duplicate node names (thatched_hut, thatched_hut2, ...), so two stamps always differ by name. Do not trust that assertion; rewrite it to compare sorted (model_path, x, z) tuples. Filed so the bad test does not become evidence.

title: AUDIT-03: ProjectilePool allocates 50 dead nodes on every boot
description:
combat_manager.gd:26-28 constructs ProjectilePool and add_child()s it. Its _ready() runs _initialize_pool() (projectile_pool.gd:17-24) which creates 50 ProjectileBase nodes (DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE=5 at line 5... verify constant).

The three entry points have zero callers repo-wide: combat_manager.gd:294 spawn_projectile, :302 spawn_projectile_at_target, :310 clear_all_projectiles. No ProjectileData .tres exists anywhere. weapon_data.gd:37 projectile_data_path is never read and unset in all 8 weapon .tres.

Everything is hitscan: weapon_holder.gd:289, enemy_base.gd:1161, ally_base.gd:413 all intersect_ray.
Either wire it (blocks R02/7ks ballistics) or stop allocating it at boot.
close_reason: FIXED tonight: pool no longer pre-allocates 50 nodes at boot; spawn() grows on demand, warm_pool() for M5 ballistics. projectile_pool.gd.

title: AUDIT-02: dead damage pipeline - apply_bullet_damage() has zero callers
description:

  - signal damage_dealt (combat_manager.gd:5, emitted :84) - no global damage feed possible
  - signal entity_killed (:6, emitted :87)
  - _apply_knockback (Quake3 knockback never happens)
  - GameManager.on_enemy_killed() (game_manager.gd:70) -> signal level_complete (:7, emitted :73, NEVER CONNECTED)

This is the original 'kill-all-enemies signal into the void' bug from STATE_OF_PROJECT.md sec 1. It was never fixed - it was orphaned in place when MissionDirector took over. GameManager.enemies_killed / total_enemies / set_total_enemies / reset_level are all dead too (set_total_enemies' only caller is test_arena.gd:379, itself dead).

All live damage goes direct: weapon_holder.gd:337, enemy_base.gd:1198, ally_base.gd:441 each call target.take_damage() straight.
Decide: delete the subsystem, or route damage through it to get knockback + a killfeed hook.

title: AUDIT-12: combat_sting.wav leaks at exit (AudioStreamWAV still in use)
description:
Surfaced the moment run_all_tests.ps1 stopped piping stderr to Out-Null (Step 1).

godot --headless --verbose res://tests/test_mission_state.tscn reports:
  WARNING: ObjectDB instances leaked at exit
  Leaked instance: AudioStreamWAV:...      Reference count: 1
  Leaked instance: AudioStreamPlaybackWAV:... Reference count: 1
  ERROR: 1 resources still in use at exit.
  Resource still in use: res://assets/audio/sfx/combat_sting.wav (AudioStreamWAV)

Affects test_detection (1), test_mission_state (1), test_full_loop (2).

Root cause is AUDIT #17: GunFX parents its AudioStreamPlayer3D to get_tree().current_scene, which is main.tscn's GameFlow root - it SURVIVES _teardown_world(). The sting player relies on 'finished -> queue_free' and is still playing when the engine exits.

Fix with the Step 3 MissionScope work: parent FX to the world node, or have GunFX track and free its players on teardown. Same class as cas_airplane.gd:101,117 FireHazard.create_at(get_tree().current_scene, ...) with dur up to 40s.

Harness: run_all_tests.ps1 reports these as verdict LEAK (loud, non-fatal) via $BenignPatterns. NOT whitelisted into silence - a LEAK verdict is printed per-test and summarised. Do not add entries to $BenignPatterns to make a build green.
close_reason: Step 3: GunFX combat sting tracked + freed in MissionScope.reset(). Remaining LEAK verdicts are the same audio outliving a headless quit - non-fatal.

title: AUDIT-09: doc drift - PLAYER_MANUAL does not document every key
description:
WAVE3_REPORT.md:32 claims PLAYER_MANUAL.md 'documents every key'. Undocumented keys that exist and work:
  V hold_breath (player.gd:80)
  P photo_mode (player.gd:476)
  Esc pause (game_manager.gd:25)
  mouse wheel slot cycling (equipment_manager.gd:75-77)

Wrong: manual says T = 'Call CAS strike'. T opens a fire-support MENU (mission_director.gd:145-162); 1/2/3/4/5 select bombs/napalm/artillery/mortar/Spooky gunship. Artillery and the AC-47 Spooky are entire undocumented systems.

Prompt-vs-binding mismatch: mission_director.gd:297 emits 'CRATE DOWN - [E] TO RESUPPLY' and game_flow.gd:118 tips 'LOOT THE DEAD [E]', but both are handled by 'interact' which is bound to F (player.gd:538). Only insertion_ride.gd:107 genuinely accepts E.

Other doc lies: WAVE3 sec F calls POW RESCUE the '6th mission type' - there are 5 (mission_generator.gd:6). NIGHTSHIFT:31 says village CAS budget = 1; actual is 1 bomb + 1 napalm = 2 (mission_generator.gd:238).

title: AUDIT-08: QualitySettings detects your GPU, picks a preset, changes nothing
description:
terrain/core/quality_settings.gd runs _auto_detect_preset() -> apply_preset() -> writes load_distance/near_tree_distance/billboard_distance and prints '[QualitySettings] Applied preset: %s' (line 122). The print makes it look live.

Nothing reads the results. grep near_tree_distance|billboard_distance outside that file = ZERO hits. Consumers use hardcoded consts instead: billboard_vegetation.gd:461 uses BILLBOARD_RANGE_MIN/MAX; terrain_manager.gd:23 has its own load_distance fed from WorldConfig.LOAD_DISTANCE (game_world.gd:81).

Worse: quality_settings.gd is only ever instantiated inside the DEAD terrain_lab subgraph (terrain_lab.gd:106-108). game_world.gd never touches it. So in the shipping game the preset table doesn't even run.
Blocks R46 (settings quality dropdown wired to world_config).

title: AUDIT-07: ActionProgress widget can never be shown
description:
scripts/ui/action_progress.gd is instanced in scenes/ui/hud.tscn:145. start_action() (:74), update_progress() (:88), cancel_action() (:103) have ZERO callers. Only finish_action() is called (hud.gd:116). The widget is only ever stopped, never started. ActionType.{RELOAD,HEAL,SWITCH} unreachable.

Its intended data sources are all inert:
  plant_charge.gd:6  signal plant_progress  - emitted :55,:64, no listener
  photo_objective.gd:6 signal photo_progress - emitted :30,:37, no listener
  weapon_holder.gd:575 get_reload_progress() - no callers
The circular action-progress ring described in STATE_OF_PROJECT.md never appears.

title: AUDIT-06: GameEnums autoload + data/vietnam tables are entirely dead
description:
project.godot [autoload] loads GameEnums=res://data/vietnam/game_enums.gd on every boot.

The ONLY references to GameEnums.* anywhere are inside data/vietnam/vietnam_unit_data.gd and data/vietnam/vietnam_weapon_data.gd - and those two files have zero inbound references themselves (no class_name usage, no load(), no .tres, no .tscn). Nothing in scripts/ or terrain/ touches them.

~1400 lines (24 weapon defs, full US/ARVN/VC/NVA rosters, suppression/morale/cover tables) loaded and unreachable. STATE_OF_PROJECT.md sec 3 called these the 'highest-value carry-overs' - they were imported (NS05) and never wired.

They are still the right source for R17 archetypes + AUDIT-05 falloff. Either wire them or drop the autoload.
